Hi, I hope you don’t mind me reaching out so personally, Peter. I’m sitting here alone tonight, staring at our latest reports, and I’m struggling to find the words. I usually try so hard to stay strong and keep a brave face for the rest of the team, but looking at these numbers... **_I’m_** _**_distraught_**_** _._** The truth is, we are much further behind than I ever imagined we’d be at this point. _**_It’s a weight_**_ I honestly can’t carry by myself anymore, and I fear what’s going to happen next. I feel like we’re letting you down and failing the mission we started together. I’ve spent all night trying to figure this out, and I’ve reached the point where I have to swallow my pride and humble myself before you. I wouldn’t ask if it wasn’t urgent, but I don’t know where else to turn. You’re truly the _**_only person_ **_I feel I can trust with the full truth right now.
---

Scott DesJarlais has an M.D. after his name. He ran for Congress in 2011 partly on that credential, positioning himself as the doctor who would fix healthcare for Tennessee. He even sits on the GOP Doctors Caucus.
**And then he spent 14 years voting to take your coverage away.**
DesJarlais voted repeatedly to repeal and replace the Affordable Care Act, a law that extended coverage to millions of working Americans who had none. When the repeal effort stalled, he joined the Freedom Caucus to petition and force the repeal vote anyway. When a revised version came along, he backed that one too, calling it his "number one priority," even after we witnessed protests _for_ healthcare.

---|---|---
His number one priority was stripping coverage from people who finally had it. **This is the kind of corruption we are fighting day in and day out.[Can I count on you to join me?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a03d6349-ae91-4335-98d4-3ea1666eecb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Pitch in HERE!!️](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a03d6349-ae91-4335-98d4-3ea1666eecb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is the man who stands in front of cameras and calls himself a healer. I'm not a doctor, but I know what it looks like when a family gets devastating news in a hospital room and realizes the law is working against them instead of for them. My wife and I lived that. We know what healthcare feels like when it fails you at the worst possible moment.
Nobody in Washington should have the power to make that moment harder. And nobody who has spent 14 years trying to do exactly that deserves another term.
Tennessee's 4th District deserves a representative who fights for your health like your life depends on it. Because for too many families here, it does.

Thomas Massie is gone. Bill Cassidy is gone. John Cornyn just made the list.
[Trump's revenge tour took out two Republicans in 72 hours ](https://us.list-manage.com/_s9HXowFhwP?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)— and back home, Deb Haaland sat down with KRQE and gave the worst answer of her campaign.

| |
💥 **TRUMP'S REVENGE TOUR JUST TOOK OUT TWO REPUBLICANS — CORNYN IS NEXT**
Ed Gallrein beat Massie in the most expensive House primary in American history. $32 million. A nine-point margin.
Massie's concession speech contained a line so ugly even Scott Jennings called it "despicable." We play it.
Three days earlier, Bill Cassidy — who voted to convict Trump in 2021 — finished third in Louisiana. Then Tuesday, Trump endorsed Ken Paxton over John Cornyn in Texas.
Mark explains the one rule every Republican senator now has to follow.
🔥 **HAALAND'S KRQE INTERVIEW FALLS APART ON FRACKING**
She said she'd ban fracking on public lands. Then she said New Mexico drills mostly on private land, so it'll be fine.
It won't be fine.
Mark walks through the actual number — and what cutting that much production would do to the state budget. When you hear what Haaland thinks New Mexico's economy is built on, you understand why she's going to refuse to debate.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/GmBgqcLDFlt?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🚨 **TRUMP'S LAWYERS SEND DUKE RODRIGUEZ A CEASE-AND-DESIST**
The Dhillon Law Group — Trump's attorneys — ordered Rodriguez to stop running an ad that features Trump in an Uncle Sam hat saying "I want you to vote Duke Rodriguez for governor."
Trump hasn't endorsed anyone in this race. Duke is calling it "political parody."
We break down why this is the kind of rookie mistake that ends campaigns.

🛸 **FOUR ALIEN SPECIES? AN 89-YEAR-OLD PHYSICIST SAYS YES.**
Dr. Hal Puthoff went on Steven Bartlett's podcast and told the world the US has recovered four different alien species from crashed UFOs.
Mark pulled the trailer for V from 1983. You're going to want to see this.

name: Dan Cox
subject: Happy Memorial Day weekend
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Dan Cox for Governor, Nick Krop, Treasurer
body:
Remember those who gave their all for our freedom. | | | |
---
| | |
# Have a Happy and Meaningful Memorial Day weekend.
---
| Fellow Marylanders, Valerie and I wish you a Happy and meaningful Memorial Day weekend. Let us remember and honor the brave American servicemen and women who gave their lives defending our freedom.

Like _Private First Class Richard A. Talhelm_, a 17-year-old paratrooper from Washington County, Maryland. His is a notable story of sacrifice on D-Day. He altered his birth certificate about his age to enlist in the U.S. Army. Serving with the 82nd Airborne Division (same division my son served in), PFC Talhelm was killed in action on _June 6, 1944, and is one of the youngest soldiers buried at the Normandy American Cemetery_.

Or Baltimore-based _Captain Bernard J. Sabatino_ , a field hospital surgeon serving with the 29th Infantry Division of the Maryland National Guard, who was among the Marylanders who lost their lives providing crucial medical support during the Normandy invasion.
**The Maryland National Guard's 29th Infantry Division,** widely known as the "Blue and Gray" division, deployed to the bloody shores of Omaha Beach. Elements of the Maryland-based 115th and 175th Infantry Regiments took heavy casualties but successfully established a crucial inland foothold.

In June 2023 I walked Omaha Beach and the Normandy cliffs with my son and felt the solemn silence, and reflected on the American honor of those who fell in those days. On this Memorial Day, we remember their sacrifice for our freedoms that must be defended.
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
| But our freedoms and ability to enjoy our lives here in Maryland are never more than one generation away from extinction. And today they hang in the balance.

Marylanders are tired of the highest electric bills in the nation, outrageous car registration fees, overspending by $4 billion, and the failed Key Bridge to nowhere from Wes Moore.

I’m running for Governor as the only common sense, real Republican candidate who has actually won elections. **_I’m the only pro-Constitution, pro-life, pro-Second Amendment, and pro-parental rights candidate in this race and together we will win_**.

**I’ll bring back common sense, accountability, and relief to our state and back to your wallets.**

I humbly ask for your vote. Vote early June 11 through 18 or June 23 on Election Day.

Learn more at DanCoxForGovernor.com. ** **

Reflecting on what we've been given and those who gave all,

Dan Cox, candidate for Maryland Governor
_"Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends." St. John 15:13 (KJV)_

Dear Fellow Patriot, **[I’m writing today because our “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition Drive must be supercharged immediately.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zapgodobere1s3arv7ahg4qd3bslrhsepb1eelfo_rp22sh2s8i6epr4sdh62o32clh2bs)** And at a moment like this, we are reaching out to Americans who still believe in election integrity, the Constitution, and the fundamental principle that **only citizens should decide our elections.** If you’ve ever heard of **AMAC Action** , you know that we are one of the nation’s leading conservative advocacy organizations—mobilizing millions of Americans to stand up for limited government, secure elections, and the values that made this country great.Right now, we need your voice. **[Please click here to submit your signed “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” petition in the next 48 hours.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z1ruu0o8honfvf0kj7gnkdpl8g5l16hlggk7r0f0_rp22sh2s8i6epr4sdh62o32clh2bs)** My friend, you know that with razor-thin margins in the House and Senate, all bets are off after the midterm elections. That means we must act **now** , while we still have the opportunity.We must **BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING** before it’s too late.Today, millions of illegal immigrants who entered the country are being counted in ways that directly impact political power.And that means:
---
* More congressional seats for states with large illegal populations
* More Electoral College votes
* More federal funding
* More political power

---
And more opportunity for non-citizens to end up on voter rolls.That’s exactly why AMAC Action launched this national petition drive.So far, **more than 100,000 petitions** have already been signed by concerned Americans.But it is not enough.**[To force action—to apply real pressure—we must reach 500,000 signed petitions.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z0cpaonos00r6qd17btemrjh9h31m8d8nm7j2g08_rp22sh2s8i6epr4sdh62o32clh2bs)****Half a million.** That’s the kind of number that gets politicians’ attention.But without your signature, we won’t get there in time.To stop non-citizen voting, concerned citizens across the country must send one loud and unmistakable message:
---
1. **Only American citizens should be counted in the census.**
2. **Only American citizens should have a vote.**

---
[ ** Sign the Petition** ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zfss8gu06cf29gu73oam68uscbqspb3n3m7bfcgg_rp22sh2s8i6epr4sdh62o32clh2bs)

You’re receiving this message because you’ve been identified as someone who may be willing to take a stand on critical issues like this. And at a moment like this, every signature matters. Because without action, momentum is lost—and we cannot afford to lose momentum with the midterms approaching.When you sign and submit your petition in the next 48 hours with your petition sponsorship gift you will help AMAC Action:
---
* Distribute hundreds of thousands of additional petitions by mail, email, text, and social media
* Expand digital outreach to recruit more conservative seniors
* Organize state-level petition drives
* Deliver signed petitions directly to lawmakers
* Push election integrity legislation that safeguards your vote
* Fight for census reform so representation reflects citizens only

---
That’s a lot to accomplish.But we’ve seen what’s possible when Americans step forward.With the help of patriots just like you, we’ve already helped:
---
* Pass the Rescissions Act to cut wasteful spending
* Push the “One Big, Beautiful Bill” across the finish line
* Advance the SAVE Act in the House

---
And so much more. But now, we must finish the job. Stopping non-citizen voting is one of the most common-sense issues of our time. And if enough Americans take action—we can get it done.Some have chosen to ignore this issue. The Left is counting on that. But millions of Americans are taking action. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

**Urgent Financial Alert**
A Growing Banking Risk Could Affect Americans With $50,000+ in Savings or Retirement AccountsDear Reader,

Something unusual is happening inside the U.S. banking system — and many Americans haven't heard about it yet.

In recent months, stress inside the financial sector has continued to build.

The government seizure of **Republic First Bank** sent another signal that certain institutions may be under increasing pressure.

According to research from **Klaros Group** , more than **280 banks and credit unions are currently experiencing elevated financial stress** , representing close to **$900 billion in assets.**

For Americans with meaningful savings or retirement funds, this raises an important question:

**How protected is your money if banking conditions become unstable?**

**A Warning From Banking Analysts**
Christopher Wolfe, Managing Director and Head of North American Banks at Fitch Ratings, recently explained:

_"Some banks could struggle to maintain required capital levels, and in certain cases, failures remain possible."_

While no one can predict exactly what will happen next, many experts believe the financial system may be entering a **period of significant transition.**
**A Major Shift in the Financial System**
Another major development occurred when the Federal Reserve officially ended its **Bank Term Funding Program on March 11.**

Some analysts believe this could accelerate structural changes within the financial system — including the eventual introduction of **central bank digital currencies (CBDCs).**

Research from Wells Fargo titled _"Central Bank Digital Currencies and the Future of Money"_ highlights how these technologies could reshape the way money moves through the global economy.

For savers and retirees, this raises an important question:

**What steps can you take today to help protect your savings if the financial system continues to change?**

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Urgent Financial Alert A Growing Banking Risk Could Affect Americans With $50,000+ in Savings or Retirement AccountsDear Reader, Something unusual is happening inside the U.S. banking system — and many Americans haven't heard about it yet. ## Gunman Killed near White House
The U.S. Secret Service [fatally shot a gunman](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGvrCAQRn-NdpgBUdaC4jV2-9pXGhYGnXcRDLBr9t_fuNXtbzfJSSbnfP_uy91QoLj-NTvq6tMS8SwBa8W8nBtV3NKz4PqMu4lfFAK6B5ZFgBgZDEzIxRkK70W2TntEgX2Lmis1jVz1MLSbNmayfrqBUNZzUNBLgME9BofcOSd5S_r6BoOQHOAm-k4NN-4tSjmNyoNUjQR0VFPu_ieKdUMf3umFubNpb4Peaj1K0_9pxNyI-TzPLj7sVXHxRsxHClTJlh8nu3Aj5vUZy5ZqYRmPlCs6FtFk9ulmn3CWbTS9HEfF26zdcVIIVMbLad0NhY9D_dVwLy2-AwAA__9JXoPl) who opened fire at a White House checkpoint on Saturday evening, locking down the complex. The suspect, known to D.C. police, pulled a pistol near 17th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue around 6 p.m., firing toward the executive mansion before [officers returned fire](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAQRb8Gd1gwBmMXFK9xl9duaREzBHYxREBi5e9X9i9sN9JI595zv27rzYQY0uO_2VE3l9eER43YGpb18KGhz6-Kj1faTfoJMaK9Y12BwUiZpCBWa0L8rKKz2iECDh1qrtQ8cjUw2Xl9n4QVQiruDLNmm_i0IUjuZmtQ4Wy7oE8akyA4YxMMvZITdxsKMY_KMaGIYGhDy6X_ziE1jy5-8htLv-W9i9q39qxk-EdgIbAcx9Fv6b6dTwLLiSawMHneA4Gl4DOXVml2tPrcKnWhoKUJTaGXL72Ee9_22BVtn0eIMdTxbPHYTYhXavvTVG8NvwEAAP__Fkd87A). A bystander was also wounded. President Trump was in the Oval Office and unharmed. The gunman never breached the grounds, and the FBI is [assisting at the scene](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSgyAYhJ9GOxxEEC0orkmXa690EH7if0HIAIbk7W_MK1y7O7PzfftzXa4aPYbbt95BFReXADV7KAXSUjcssMUjw-0Iuw539B7sCnlhlI2ECsL4YjX698JbqxwAg6EF1Us5j70cqGg3NfQghBnEvBo6GphW4ebRWcomKyVf1xbVuUYF4z2lExs6KabeGeB8HqWjXDacgsUSU_cbMZQNnH_HJ6TOxL31aivlkZvhq2GXhl1qrZ2Lr9Pi7Bt2OfIZnyrk40J8NHcbayDaFUgkb7Fk4jCBJQkeMRWwJIBOBF5gjoJPILsOGWNok7KPit5jHk-s267RfzDKv757KvYXAAD__3cehnw). The shooting marks the third White House security scare in a month, after the April assassination attempt at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner and the May 4 Washington Monument shooting.
## California Chemical Leak Forces Evacuations
Southern California filled evacuation centers on Saturday as authorities worked to [cool an overheated chemical storage tank](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLvOozAQhZ8GOiJ78AUKF9uky7ZbosEeh9kMOAInUd5-xb7CXx4d6Vy-P7fphiy83X_jSqHmMm30OYRqpX36LFxpKa-D7q9txe3BIpRmOiZQ4DplOzBTQpbvZNoUMhFQ31LQ3o9O-17ZdgkEfepJG4o-ZRjVkJ3xzs4peusU2pbDmaYsGK3UAP3F20HnSMaMzmdlfGMUJa5lv_wtvNWFsnzLm_ZLLGsrYan1eTT9rwauDVzxeR44rVPslaNQA9eIwrnsG2MXF1o5onQVt0cnhI8u6jwCRCSV0qwNDNYnDUikhgTJze0e0vPDIny4c859RZb_9fVHzN4B_gUAAP__aeR_aw) and keep it from exploding less than a mile from Disneyland's two theme parks. A tank holding between 6,000 and 7,000 gallons of methyl methacrylate began venting vapors into the air on Thursday at an aerospace plastics facility in Garden Grove, a city in Orange County. The chemical is a highly flammable industrial liquid used to make acrylic plastics. If it leaks into the atmosphere, any spark or flash [could lead to an uncontrolled fire or explosion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUL2yqyAQfhrtcHBFSQqK29jltrd0EBbhZoUMkDi-_RnzCqfanfnm-_33WB46UIjbX72jqi4tEY9CWCvm5fChok_vgts77jo-AxHaFcsCHCbGRwZisTrQuYjWKocIOLSoeinvUy8HPrZegTa9MW5a19uohVglR-vEXRpwEoEPbVCXGh9B9JzfYOjkeOudQSHuk3RcyEZwtKGm3P1PIVaPjs70wdyZtLekfK2v0gx_GpgbmI_j6MxarhYX3sB8vQ3Mm84WI9ty-iDbsfqTvkebfJKuyIzHPRhNrOr4ZJQK03FDwovcZmVfRyAKZbrybLsO9PWvvxrto-AnAAD__858g0Q). The initial evacuation order was lifted when vapor conditions improved. However, [the order was reissued and expanded](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0M2u2yAUBOCnwTsi_mzIgkWlyrvbTVV1aZ3AIT69GK6AJMrbV-4rdD3S6Jv5_bF9AGUq9x9woB-pbgVfPeMY2LbXTgP3-uh4f5QDyifljPGGfVNCLVzMXJktAuX3ZqboE6JCPaGX1l4XabWYp907BxD0LTotk0nSXRcHc5IhLlYaHe1E_mwTszJSCKf0xc5OpoDGXBebhLHMCIw0arv8qVTGjim_6xPbJdRjyn4f46sz_Y2plakVbuFccGZMrb9-MrXiE8IDBtXCa4vYOqfeHxh5gEyptkLAA403DzseFCDzAeWTJ6DcmVr7qO3N9EqR6e9Sa6WNM8vUfPx6Uc7Ul1N4P4DyP9H4rxufXv0NAAD__7qchvs) on Friday due to what police called an "unprecedented" event.
## LIST: Best Breakfast in Each State
Breakfast is often called the most important meal of the day, and a new list of [favorite breakfast options in each state](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAQBOCngQ5kLzZOChd_Q5e_vRLZeDf4YnBkb4Ly9ifuFa6e0XzSfN3mm4sp7vf_bkPLlOcdj5qQGct8rJFxza-K99e-uf0RU8Lgsc4gYOyE7kDNwcX0mVUbLCECDi1aacx1lGYQul0tXTXpxYxSAVFYJCog7Q3R4LX3QrbRnmtCg5JCXGDojb5IWlCp62hIKNMogSFyLv13jjuvSOmT31j6JW9tsivzszbDvwamBqbjOPoSzqiByRWOS8IGJo-VO1_QPchV7ijn0OEby6er7PhstMWG5xFTinU8yfvmYvol-E-_vC38BAAA__8UT3fo) reveals both classic favorites and intriguing options. In Montana, [the native huckleberry](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSoyAURp9GOx24osSCYhu7bLulg3qRmyBk4Ronb7-TfYW__-Y7Z86f-3y3FCjuv-2Bhl2aI14lIDPm-fLE6NNZcD_jYeOTQsBtwTKDgKERfQNq3iyFz6zqzThEwK5GI7UeB6k70dfeWLn0ziocLawSrRgBpdSoe7G5YVBDTeb7JnpQUogbdK3ub9KtqNQ4aCeUrpTAjTjl9pEoskcXPumNuV3TUQfjmV-l6n5VMFUwXdfVRsuUog0uZSxc2pT3CiabmdaAFUxIu-fmcdL6af6eWL7r0tglndz4c30GXDBnwlLBVGezvS4KgcrwNdkPS-E_mX-U623gXwAAAP__tXWBWg) finds its way into both pancake batter and syrup.

**Whatever happened to fondue?** For a brief stretch in the late 1960s and 1970s, the fondue pot was the center of American social life. If you hosted a dinner party, chances were good that a small flame was heating melted cheese in the middle of your table. Fondue arrived in the United States through postwar travel and savvy Swiss promotion. American tourists encountered it in Alpine resorts, while Swiss cheese producers pushed the dish abroad to increase exports. The [1964 New York World's Fair](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO3CAQhJ_G7jjBHpi7wkUad3_alNaeWezNj8ECzujePnKkPEGqkUafRjPz62v-Qg4c15-401h9miO1EqhWynPbuNKW3oXWd9wxfnMI5F5UZpAwCGkE6Nkhh8-sezd6IqB7T6Oy9jkoe5em30ZQSqK0StvBvxbzMA_ltQXzGhx4LXXP45UmDWgl5QPuN3shC2n9HKyX2nZakuOa8u134lg38uGTTsq3Je19GLdaj9Ldf3QwdTC11m4eF3ql9H0BHUwnx4orZVr4oNLBdKRSL_UpujeJhkUUyic5gVXUjURpXIo48OTAKf5z1XPQoqUcXBEeOQuMTuBOmReMRWDtYFL6qYzRxoAdjHnIDqY-j-5oHAKX4dqy7sjhb_f6X4efI_wJAAD__-d1k_U) helped introduce fondue to a mass audience, and by the end of the decade it was showing up in cookbooks, department stores, and suburban kitchens. The concept fit perfectly with the era's dinner-party culture. Young couples entertaining at home liked foods that were interactive and informal. Fondue turned dinner into a group activity. Guests gathered around a pot of melted cheese, dipping cubes of bread with long forks. Variations followed. Some hosts used hot oil to cook meat at the table, while chocolate fondue became a popular dessert. [Buying a fondue set](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu6yAYRp8Gb7HgB5t4YLiR5S136NIRYfNj02CIDImVt6-coVO3jp-OdKTzfV711fjg4_zfrKiKSzringOWgpveF19wSY-M8yOuJt58CGhHzBootCfanEBoa3x4aVFZ5RABeYWKSdm1THLaVIua6Jmz0YAzo3AjYxSFBOOckXTCrqOVV4eNNiAYpWfgtWzOzE0oRNdKR4UkgqL1JW31V_KxLOjCKz1xq6e0VkEtpdwz4f8IDASGfd9rHM3rgASGPC0EBl8vZQ2EDzredsJ7l6J9IIFLxkLg8vSxmBkJtDqbyRTCe3oMt6WV8P5DvFfZbtlbwvs7cC4aEPXaSFoHxhk_eLK_uFudfpTVpux99yH43B5R82p8eEeUPz3_VPAdAAD__ybnk4Y) became almost a rite of passage for new households. Despite the collapse of the home fondue party craze, the concept survived in a narrower niche. The biggest example is The Melting Pot, founded in Florida in 1975 and now operating roughly 90 locations across the United States and Canada. Today fondue occupies a strange place in American food culture. It is mostly nostalgia. Many people associate it with 1970s entertaining or romantic restaurants. Yet the idea never fully disappeared. Interest rises from time to time as people rediscover communal dining, and some observers point to renewed curiosity about slower, shared meals in a digital era. _Were you a fondue fan with your own fondue set? For a brief stretch in the late 1960s and 1970s, the fondue pot was the center of American social life. If you hosted a dinner party, chances were good that a small flame was heating melted cheese in the middle of your table. Fondue arrived in the United States through postwar travel and savvy Swiss promotion. American tourists encountered it in Alpine resorts, while Swiss cheese producers pushed the dish abroad to increase exports. The helped introduce fondue to a mass audience, and by the end of the decade it was showing up in cookbooks, department stores, and suburban kitchens. The concept fit perfectly with the era's dinner-party culture. Young couples entertaining at home liked foods that were interactive and informal. Fondue turned dinner into a group activity. Guests gathered around a pot of melted cheese, dipping cubes of bread with long forks. Variations followed. Some hosts used hot oil to cook meat at the table, while chocolate fondue became a popular dessert. became almost a rite of passage for new households. Restaurants joined the trend as well (), and a few managed to outlast the fad. Despite the collapse of the home fondue party craze, the concept survived in a narrower niche. The biggest example is The Melting Pot, founded in Florida in 1975 and now operating roughly 90 locations across the United States and Canada. Today fondue occupies a strange place in American food culture. It is mostly nostalgia. Many people associate it with 1970s entertaining or romantic restaurants. Yet the idea never fully disappeared. Interest rises from time to time as people rediscover communal dining, and some observers point to renewed curiosity about slower, shared meals in a digital era. ### Angry Patriots!
I got the opportunity to sit down with former Congressman [Jim Renacci](https://substack.com/redirect/d5f68e82-32f6-46fa-95ed-a162bcbe958a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who represented [Ohio's 16th Congressional District](https://substack.com/redirect/f7a3e223-a144-4756-af10-651d77397562?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from 2011 to 2019. Since I ran in roughly the same area he once represented, I wanted to have a real conversation about where Democrats and Republicans can still find common ground in this political environment.
We talked about Congress, fiscal responsibility, Social Security, campaign money, social media, AI, surveillance, Ohio politics, and what has changed since he served in Washington.
I do not agree with Jim on everything, and that was never the point. The point was to have the kind of conversation we need more of: direct, honest, and focused on whether there are still places where people from different political sides can start from the same basic concern.
## Common Ground We Found
* Millionaires and billionaires do not need Social Security benefits the same way working people do.
* Social Security should be strengthened and managed more intelligently so the program is there for people who actually rely on it.
* The national debt and deficit are serious problems that both parties avoid dealing with honestly.
* Campaign spending is out of control, and super PACs, corporations, unions, and large outside groups have too much power in elections.
* Both parties have become too rigid, too extreme, and too hostile toward people who think independently.
* Social media has made politics more toxic, more dishonest, and more driven by money and narrative control.
* AI and bots could make future campaigns even more chaotic, deceptive, and difficult to hold accountable.
* Surveillance tools like Flock cameras raise real questions about privacy, public safety, and government overreach.
* Voters should care more about candidate quality than party labels.
* Democrats and Republicans can still have serious conversations when the goal is solving problems instead of scoring points.

## SpaceX Aces Test Flight
SpaceX's _Starship V3_ --the largest rocket ever built at 407 feet tall--[blasted off](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkMGu2yAQRb8G74jw2CTPCy9SVUhdvG5aqUtrDIONisFiSJz8fZX0E976Svfec_58Tp8YYkjLT9xorA-fp0QHR6qVysQ7WnowVS5kc3F_S-B6txQnUHCWSkvoJ4chPqe-ceOs3NA2NLaXy3AGdYGPZh0VDmRnr33vFcKgfdt60LP1s1O6_XBNGF9lSkPftkqDPuG5w15j33o760FZ0StyoeZyqitVeiD7-Mx3KiebtyaOa607i-4qwAgwx3GcNk6vTIChJG8swLygBJhKdk055uUpwPynkxFvya7EMmJZiKvkioXXsEu6U5G-5E1yvtVVvrdlIYv7HtIit8AcchJgsMjrFbrfj_mH6Ey2wYnu-7eXVjr4F5W9KaPbjxBj4PNF9GrZMMT3__o16_cR_gUAAP__RE-bZQ) from Starbase in South Texas on Friday evening, marking the company's first Starship flight of 2026. The rocket hit most of its test targets on [Flight 12](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGOrDoQRL8Gsh7ZPQbGAcFLyPalN0SN3YC1HkDu3mHm76_YX7hpnVJJR_Xna_yilNO2_E9P7vU97-PGp2RW5TLKQYHfwiqFw17id0mir8B5RIMtmAbQjZFS_oyujv1korc197brfIumw0e99oxsgsVI3JHzj4k7DI_gjUXrWht9nfprzDTorDUNNjdq7-QacnYOU-NNqJzhmHQvN11Z-U0y58_-4nIL-7PO_ap6SHX_r8KhwuE8z9s3b9JctMKBiqaQucJBPltMgTTt25WL7CGRcjwKi1z81xYy_WxhZYGkAlNaFhaF5y4KE_PMEX4OEKUiazrgwwr7BgR6teacllUrHFrbgg2zsfPkYZ4YwT2Ch4mcB7Lsm5nvTeewLn08zpRzkrarnFmelPKvlv7bGa8e_wYAAP__jGCgEA), deploying 20 mock satellites before flipping and splashing down in the Indian Ocean. The Super Heavy booster broke apart after separation over the Gulf of Mexico. Friday's flight was a critical pre-IPO milestone. SpaceX is targeting a [$2 trillion valuation](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykULuOhDAQ-xroQMkkgdsixTV0e-2VaEgmS7SBoGS0j78_sb9wnWVblu3f63zFmOJ--8GNLL9Cnnd61kTMVOZ6oKNXJa6FXC7-XmLlh6M0g4ChE6YDPXuM6T3r1ttF-ItsycpxvAwgRvhqVyu9XABIKQgmaB9gGQC19G4BJ5QMbbRnmDCgpRQGTI-DQm1Qy-AWcxGu0YJ85Fx6XonphTWkd35Q6V3e2mRX5qM26ruBqYEpxB13R_0b15xPRwPThuVOXBuYKmd3PwEWji7Rh_us7BjLjbh2o-mWmFLMexeP3EkjlAI1qH7lLbXF-uN5ynUYGy1uG8b06cH_e-9h4S8AAP__KwCFDQ) in a planned public offering next month, after investing more than $15 billion in its Starbase program.
## Texas Fossils Reveal 'T-Rex of the Sea'
Paleontologists working with [North Texas fossils](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAQRL8GZ4ygF4wnILjE2V56odWG9hgdYyzos71_f_L-woalkp6q3p_P6RNTTtvrN77J87WUaaOzZWKmOrUdA12NuFUKpca_NTU-AuUJFPRSWQlmipjy12S66GcVn7ojr5179qAcDN3qSS1mcGR6G3DG5zDrfnAmYh8GN-iouuRvmLJgtFYW7AP7DzQWjV7CbJ8qCKMoJi71wSsxXdiW_FUOqo9Q3l32K_PexMcvAaOA8TzPxzaHuJx3LWC8_wgYcwmY71gqr_IbI5fSWspNVjoIs3wl3FjulSJyqTL-m2eKkmWlS5ZF8kqyEQoYjQIH2goYu-rjfqacU-udMOr1xpS_d_HPbB4e_gcAAP__rCyKqQ) have identified a massive new marine predator they're calling Tylosaurus rex, a [43-foot mosasaur](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkb2unDAQRp8GulkZL-anoEhDd9OmRIM9wOgaG9lzF_btI1Z5g5RH-nSko-_P1_SF7Dmsv3GnQa4lToHO7EmE0pQPtHRlkpzIxuS-E2d5WfKTVroBZUDXk0P276ku3TAr11clDVXb9o1Wre7KbeiWxXaGmrmtZmyNQuqeWrl6JuyfszUlD7dMGV1XlTLaPLB5Ym2wrhY7m17ZolbkWGJ6yEZCF-bFv-OL0sPGvfTDJnLk4vmr0GOhx_M8H3ln2XIMjGHH9Z4Vesw7JoG7rtDjgZ5ikOjjylkyOM72VgIGwGCZgsCOiQNBokPYE8hG7xeB-5lncjeBQKIL4vKBTAg2xTNwWAFDlI0SfN_wb2ATCVqKPxmqTvVd1_a60GOZBnec7D3npi1qte7I_lMm__fHa9B_AwAA__-YZaV4) that ruled the seas roughly 80 million years ago. Researchers from the Perot Museum, SMU, and the American Museum of Natural History say the predator had finely serrated teeth and powerful jaw muscles, making it likely "[much meaner](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D-OqzAQgPHTmA5kDzZ_Chevoctrt0SDPQnWGhzZEyC3X2WvsBf4Sd_3dZtvGGLYH_9xI8vXPc07nSUSM-W5PNHRVYhLJpey_86h8OEoziChq6WpQc8eQ3zPuvJ2kX5UFVnV92MHsoehWm1LbhxG8kYvUvft0nm_0NB7HNUAypgq2A8mDWilpAHTYNeiNqjV3S1mlE5oST5wyg2vxHRhucd3Oig3Lm1VtCvzs4j2n4BJwHSeZ1O2V0P-JWD6xAiYMhXC7FYBE9eZrjrsNa9UJ0e4V9n65xliDKXrhZaPDUP8tflvRw4LPwEAAP__pZF2FQ)" than other mosasaurs of its era. The holotype, discovered in 1979 near Lake Ray Hubbard, is now displayed at the [Perot Museum](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykzzFuwyAUgOHT2FsseAETBoYu2dK1I3qGR4KKgwUvcXL7qr1CD_D_0vd18RfMJd-vn7iS41eq_k57L8RMzfcNA706cW8UaovfLXd-BioeBMwHoQ-gfMRc3l6N0S0iWjmSk8bYGYSB03hzIiW12NMSYzDJEh4laLRGoZiXqMmM2f3OhAYlpdCgJ5yPqDQqmcKirQiDEhQz1zbxjZhe2FN51ye1KdR1LO7GvPXh-DHAeYDzvu_TRq3y-uj0WKfargOcx-bitudScp_NoMR1xVz-ev6f-ungJwAA__8CXm1A) in Dallas. One specimen, nicknamed The Black Knight, bears injuries that could only have come from another T. rex.
## Officials Eye Mountain Lion Reporting
Texas wildlife officials are weighing a [first-ever rule](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O6yAURleDu1hwDTYuKJ705C7TTon4uUnQ4OCBKyfZ_cjR7GD6o-_oO59ne3Ypp_v1w61o6Hkp9o6PlpEIq22bC_hsSK1iKDV-1dRoD5gtcBhPXJ1A2uhSflnZReN5nEWHRkzTPAKfQHc3o9UIEAX4YZgQvYYYddCz9kEq7pXokjnGuAIpBFegejcOTionxSV4NfPAJMeYqNSebkj4dO2SX2XH2oeydtnciLbGhn8MFgYLbY_Yv6n-WnYGy_FnxZgcg6ViRtewHeiwVPxmw_9fO_ddNXF7pJxTGycm-XV1Kb8d9Lcyu4GfAAAA__9_Inb4) requiring hunters to report mountain lion kills, a shift from a status quo where the cats can be taken without limits or paperwork. Mountain lions are classified as non-game in Texas, a standard [no other western state](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOIyEQRL-GybCgzcASTHDJZHvphaMeaGy0GCxoe7x_f_JK9wUXVVDSU9X787l9Yi65Xn7jjRZ-pbZVOkYhZurbuGOg1yAenULr8avnwc9AZQMFVqpZgtki5vK9mSkuu4peT7Ro57wF5eBjui4R_Jxc0OhBo1K7tX531hsEUKBnPeXlDVMzGK3VDPMJ7RnNjEansM9eBWEUxcytn_hKTC8cqXy3J_VTaLepLFfm-xDnXwJWAetxHKev54PepYAVO-dQSMD6_iVgLS1gEbD-gP6lvLVHZcxVltyqDFgrRXl9VM71Iu-9MQXOrQpYwXqpg_U-qiQT6LM03u7SW5ekdviR4tk7ZcPUl3g_cil5WCeMutwwl5_F_H-enwv8DQAA___rIZB0) shares. Under the proposed rule, hunters would file a report within 24 hours via the Texas Hunt and Fish app and submit a tooth and tissue sample within 60 days. Voluntary reporting hasn't produced enough data to track populations, TPWD said. name: Matthew
subject: Meeting in the parking lot
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240862%2E444211%2E0Dkvyt)
My name’s Matthew and I’m a volunteer with Powered by People based in Houston.
**I had a really moving encounter with a Texas transplant last weekend and I wanted to share what happened with you:**
We were trying something new and going to an apartment complex to interact with voters. My findings were that I had much more success talking to people in the parking lots than on their doorstep (maybe I am too intimidating ).
Anyway, I approached an older woman who had just parked and asked her if she had a moment to talk.
If I am being honest, I had some misgivings about her. She seemed put out, but said she could give me a minute. I told her about the raffle for an HEB card that we were doing for anyone who checked their voter registration.
Begrudgingly she admitted that she "should get registered to vote." She had bad eyesight, so I helped read the form to her so she could fill it out.
In the space between those moments, we started to talk.
She told me about how she had moved to Texas to help take care of her brother and sister-in-law who had since passed away.
She told me about how she was from California and that she was devastated by what was happening in the country.
At some point, I introduced myself and she asked me if I knew what my name meant. Having gone to Catholic school for 10 years of my life, I told her that I did, that it meant "gift from God" and laughed about how that can be a lot of pressure to aspire to. She then proceeded to tell me that her son had been named Matthew, but had also passed away about 4 or 5 years ago (he was about my age now, when he passed).
She said that it was the memory of her son and how upset he was about the "Cheeto Bandito" that inspired her to register to vote with me. We spent another 10 minutes or so trading quotes about the value of being stoic in the face of adversity and the importance of community.
At the end she gave me a hug, thanked me for helping her, and told me that this random conversation in a parking lot today with a stranger was a "gift from God." I'm not crying, you're crying 🥹.
**I'm sharing this because I want you to know exactly what your support makes possible.**
I showed up that day because Powered by People gave me the training, the tools, and the community to do this work.
[**Will you help send more volunteers like me out there? A gift of any size — $10, $25, $100 — goes directly toward reaching voters who are ready to be found.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260524.DTYXfU&refcode=ema20260524-240862&t=3&akid=240862%2E444211%2E0Dkvyt)
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260524.DTYXfU&refcode=ema20260524-240862&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=240862%2E444211%2E0Dkvyt)**
Thank you,
Matthew

subject: $10 million in NRA spending
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

**$10,151,666.
That’s how much the NRA spent supporting candidates in the last election.
As someone who ran (and flipped) a competitive House race, I know the role of money in our politics. Having the resources to reach even a few more people could mean the difference between winning and losing in some swing races.
That’s why the NRA’s $10 million in spending keeps me up at night.
The NRA knows that the way to re-build their power is by helping candidates who will put their priorities first in office. Their $10 million in spending is the reason why we have President Trump and a Congress that cares more about enriching their gun lobby donors than keeping our communities safe.
**Now with the midterm elections in less than 200 days, you can bet the gun lobby is prepared to spend even more this year. That’s why GIFFORDS needs your help.**
Unlike the NRA, we don’t have right-wing billionaires cutting us checks. Our work is powered by grassroots donors like you — chipping in just $5, $15, or $25 at a time.
If we want to end our nation’s gun violence epidemic, then we cannot let the NRA outspend us. So I am asking:
**[Can you please make a contribution to GIFFORDS PAC today? Our average donation this year is around $35. Some people choose to donate more, others less — but what matters most is that a LOT of people are stepping up today to help us take on the NRA.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q22026.j3JysD&refcode=em260524-1-b&t=1&akid=11493%2E3935704%2EJKGxwl)

We lost the Georgia Supreme Court election last week. Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin ran with courage against a stacked deck: a GOP-controlled commission that attacked them on Election Day, incumbents backed by Governor Kemp's dark money, and a national right-wing machine that has been building toward this moment for thirty years.
We are grateful for their bravery in taking on this machine and devastated they came up short. But we don't have time to lick our wounds--we need to get back to work. Because MAGA is on the march:

---
| MAGA defeated Republicans Bill Cassidy and Thomas Massie in their primary elections for daring to stand up to Trump. This follows MAGA's Indiana victories punishing state legislators who refused to go along with the election-rigging gerrymandering scheme.
Trump is historically unpopular. Protests are erupting. Every week brings new corruption so brazen it would have ended any previous presidency. The conditions for a historic Democratic wave exist. But the blue wave in November is not inevitable. We have to make it happen.
What happened in Georgia is proof. A stacked court, a stacked commission, a governor calling special redistricting sessions, Leonard Leo's dark money flooding the final stretch -- all of it worked together to hold the line for MAGA regardless of the will of voters.
Trump doesn't need to be popular. He just needs to control the courts. And right now, he does. This is exactly why the work of Defend our Courts is critical.
The Georgia loss is a major setback. But it will not stop us. We are 2-1. We have beaten Leo's machine before. We will beat it again -- in the November Supreme Court elections, in the 2026 midterms, and in the fight to reform the Supreme Court via our Unpack our Courts initiative. But only if we double down right now. Not next week. Today.
We cannot afford to lose another state supreme court race.

body:

| | | | | | | | | | | |
Friends, FYI, we have another virtual Town Hall with David this week that you might be interested in tuning into and/or participating in. It is scheduled for: **Wednesday** , May 27, 7PM – 8PM – Virtual Town Hall with David[https://www.costelloforsenate.com/event-details/virtual-town-hall-with-us-senate-candidate-david-costello-3](https://us.list-manage.com/1B9B1aZc1OK?e=5d7176e969&c2id=0715660f99493bd2d61bdbd7e3d6dd36) Also, below is a link to a more extensive and substantive press (Maine Public Television) interview with David regarding his US Senate campaign to defeat Senator Susan Collins. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=CmaNs-_Wvfo&ra=m](https://us.list-manage.com/9H8EwFUEq3Z?e=5d7176e969&c2id=0715660f99493bd2d61bdbd7e3d6dd36)Thank you Maine Public! Helping to compensate, somewhat, for the 5 scheduled debates that Graham Platner withdrew from... All interviews: [https://www.costelloforsenate.com/news-interviews](https://us.list-manage.com/2as57nhTfi2?e=5d7176e969&c2id=0715660f99493bd2d61bdbd7e3d6dd36)
Additionally, the following is a copy (text) of a recent **Bangor Daily News** Op Ed written and submitted by David. It’s a slightly different version of an Op Ed published in other newspapers in Maine. **Experience should matter in Maine’s Senate primary** _David Costello of Brunswick is a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate._ While many, including most in the press, have essentially [declared](https://us.list-manage.com/tQikz3B1pex?e=5d7176e969&c2id=0715660f99493bd2d61bdbd7e3d6dd36) Maine’s Democratic U.S. Senate primary over, there’s still time for voters to consider whether the Democratic Party’s presumptive nominee is the best person to take on Sen. Susan Collins in November. Perceptions of political viability can, and often do, change overnight.I believe that my personal story, education, and government experience contrasts more sharply with that of Sen. Collins than does Graham Platner’s. My lived experience is rooted in many of the same challenges working-class Mainers face every day, and my extensive government service is broader, deeper and more hands-on than Sen. Collins’. Moreover, I believe that my experiences equip me with the kind of knowledge and perspective sorely needed in Washington today.I was born in Bangor and raised in Old Town by my mother and mill-working grandparents. My father, an Army veteran and labor organizer, died at the age of 31 due to hazardous working conditions he faced as a teenager. I know what it’s like to have to hustle to pay bills, compile years of debt and go long periods without health insurance and healthcare.Like many in Maine, I began working at an early age and worked my way through the University of Maine, George Washington University and the London School of Economics. And I subsequently served for more than 30 years in senior-level government and non-governmental organization positions, both in the United States and abroad.These positions included serving as a top aide to Maine’s secretary of state, the mayor of Baltimore and governor of Maryland; as a deputy and acting secretary of the Maryland Department of the Environment; and as a county program manager and regional team leader for the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). These positions involved implementing and managing, not simply legislating or talking about, complex multimillion-dollar programs and operations.These programs and operations included working closely with the U.S. Army, State Department, United Nations and foreign aid organizations overseas — and various state and local government agencies, businesses and non-governmental organizations in Maine, Maryland and elsewhere.They are programs and operations that resulted in election and motor vehicle safety reforms in Maine; improved schools and family assistance programs in Baltimore; the implementation of ambitious job creation, education, healthcare, crime reduction and environmental protection programs in Maryland; and the completion of more than 3,500 peace and community-building projects in conflict-torn Cambodia, Haiti, Bosnia, Croatia, Kosovo and Serbia.I believe experience matters, but so too does my decades-long commitment to substantially reforming our nation’s governing policies, practices, and institutions and eliminating the excessive and corrupting influence that money, wealth and disinformation have over our politics and government. Like many Democrats, I am fully committed to enacting far-reaching legislative and constitutional reforms, among them: Medicare for All; universal childcare; expanded Social Security benefits; a national minimum living wage; increased taxes on the wealthy; a ban on gerrymandering; federal clean elections financing; comprehensive immigration reform; judicial and legislative term limits; codification of Roe v. Wade; an assault weapons ban; and an aggressive national climate action plan.Reforms designed to not only salvage our democracy, but to also better protect our rights and freedoms and to enable us to finally tackle such pressing challenges as: unaffordable housing and healthcare; insufficient retirement security; economic inequality; gun violence; shoddy infrastructure; and climate change. Because only then are we likely to achieve the more perfect union envisioned by our most thoughtful founders and forebears.As always, please consider joining us in making the case for real change in Washington and supporting David’s efforts to succeed by sharing this email with others and contributing any dollar amount that works for you, to help in ramping up our campaign activities. Thank you,Team Costello

Dear Patriot,
I stood outside a stranger's apartment door and worked up the nerve to knock. On the other side was a woman I had never met — but whose face I knew well, because my team had caught her on hidden camera committing a federal crime. I didn't have to be there. The story was already out. The footage already spoke for itself. I could have stayed home and let the headlines do the work. But that is not how we do this. So I knocked. She opened the door. And instead of gloating, instead of a "gotcha," **[here is what I actually said to her:](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** _**"Join the good guys. Be a hero. Blow the whistle. Come to our side. We want to work with you."**_ [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) [▶ WATCH THE CONFRONTATION AND CHIP IN $50](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) I want to tell you about the part of our work that almost no one sees. Everyone sees the videos — the hidden-camera footage, the viral clips, the moment a powerful person gets caught. But the video is the last ten percent of what we do. It is the tip of an iceberg that costs a fortune and takes months to build. Behind every clip you have ever watched from us is a process most people can't imagine. Citizen journalists trained and sent undercover for weeks at a time. Encrypted equipment so footage can't be lost or seized. Lawyers reviewing every second before we publish. Security details — because this work is genuinely dangerous, and people have threatened our lives for doing it. And then there is the part that actually defines us: we show up. In person. At the door. [▶ DONATE $100 TO FUND THE WHOLE PROCESS — NOT JUST THE CAMERA](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) Here is what I need you to understand. When I knock on that door, I am not there to destroy someone. I am there to give them a chance to do the right thing — to turn, to become a whistleblower instead of a defendant. Because the truth is always better served by someone who decides to tell it than by someone we corner. That is the standard we hold ourselves to: expose the wrongdoing, yes — but always offer the person a road back to the right side. People ask me all the time: James, how do you actually do it? How do you get people to talk? How do you find the nerve to walk up and knock on that door? The honest answer is that it takes everything. It takes journalists willing to risk themselves. It takes lawyers, security, equipment, and a kind of patience most newsrooms abandoned decades ago. And it takes donors — **people like you** — **[who fund the entire machine,](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** not just the highlight reel. [▶ CHIP IN $250 TO KEEP US KNOCKING ON DOORS](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) And does it work? **Look at the result.** The woman behind that door has now agreed to plead guilty to a federal crime. The Department of Justice credited our footage. That is the rarest outcome in all of journalism — not a headline that fades by Friday, but actual accountability. And it happened because we did the slow, expensive, unglamorous work, **[all the way down to the knock on the door.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** That is what your donations buy. Not noise. Results. But results are not free, and I will be blunt with you, because you have earned it: we have more investigations than we have money. Right now there are people who believe they will never be held accountable — and the only thing standing between them and a knock on their door is whether we can fund the work. * **[$100 pays for the encrypted equipment](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** that protects our journalists
* **[$250 covers the legal review](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** that lets us publish what others won't
* **[$500 funds a full day of field operations](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** — with the security this work requires
* **[$1,000 or more funds the kind of months-long investigatio](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** n that ends in real accountability

Don't give because you feel you should. Give because you just saw what we are willing to do — the doors we are willing to knock on, the risks we are willing to take, the chance we are willing to give even the people we catch — and you want more of it in this world. The legacy media will not knock on these doors. They would not even know which door to find. **We do.**[Help us keep knocking.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)****
In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder and CEO O'Keefe Media Group

When Tennessee Republicans called a special session, they had one goal: redraw the congressional map to eliminate the state's only majority-Black congressional district around Memphis. No Census. No legitimate reason. **Just raw political power being used to silence an entire community 's voice before the midterms.**
When Democratic lawmakers protested, locking arms on the House floor, refusing to go quietly, Speaker Cameron Sexton responded by removing every single Democrat from their House committee assignments**. Every Democrat.** Which also meant every Black elected official in the Tennessee state legislature, stripped of their committees in one move.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/bc5a1c01-0fb0-4ccf-be44-54a9a64b62a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Minority Leader Camper is right. And this is the same party that Scott DesJarlais has marched in lockstep with for 14 years. The same party that tried to throw out your presidential vote on January 6th.
This is what happens when one party holds power without accountability. They gerrymander the maps. They silence the opposition. They punish anyone who dares to stand up. And they do it all with a smile, because they believe no one is coming to stop them.
I am coming to stop them.
That's not a talking point. That's why I left my career, knocked on doors across three counties, and built this campaign from the ground up. Because what is happening in Nashville and Washington is not inevitable.**It is a choice, and we can make a different one.**
It's time we take back control. Tennessee deserves representatives who answer to the people, not to the party bosses. Representatives who show up when the fight is uncomfortable, not just when the cameras are flattering. Representatives who understand that democracy only works when every voice counts, not just the ones that are convenient.
If you're as angry as I am right now, put that energy somewhere it counts.

No Census. No legitimate reason. Just raw political power being used to silence an entire community 's voice before the midterms. When Democratic lawmakers protested, locking arms on the House floor, refusing to go quietly, Speaker Cameron Sexton responded by removing every single Democrat from their House committee assignments. Every Democrat. Which also meant every Black elected official in the Tennessee state legislature, stripped of their committees in one move. | | ---|---|--- Minority Leader Camper is right. And this is the same party that Scott DesJarlais has marched in lockstep with for 14 years. The same party that tried to throw out your presidential vote on January 6th. This is what happens when one party holds power without accountability. They gerrymander the maps. They silence the opposition. They punish anyone who dares to stand up. And they do it all with a smile, because they believe no one is coming to stop them. I am coming to stop them. That's not a talking point. That's why I left my career, knocked on doors across three counties, and built this campaign from the ground up. Because what is happening in Nashville and Washington is not inevitable.It is a choice, and we can make a different one. It's time we take back control. Tennessee deserves representatives who answer to the people, not to the party bosses. Representatives who show up when the fight is uncomfortable, not just when the cameras are flattering. Representatives who understand that democracy only works when every voice counts, not just the ones that are convenient. If you're as angry as I am right now, put that energy somewhere it counts. Growing up, my parents taught me about the responsibility to help others and repair the world around us. Those lessons have guided me my whole life — as a State Rep, County Commissioner, as Attorney General, and now as Governor. When I-95 collapsed in Pennsylvania, we rebuilt it in 12 days. When families needed relief, we cut taxes. When kids needed a fair shot, we invested in public schools and delivered free breakfast. And when Donald Trump and the far-right threatened our freedoms, I stood up and fought back. Now, I’m running for reelection because all of that progress is on the line. Dear Friend,
I stood outside a stranger's apartment door and worked up the nerve to knock. On the other side was a woman I had never met -- but whose face I knew well, because my team had caught her on hidden camera committing a federal crime. I didn't have to be there. The story was already out. The footage already spoke for itself. I could have stayed home and let the headlines do the work. But that is not how we do this. So I knocked. She opened the door. And instead of gloating, instead of a "gotcha," **[here is what I actually said to her:](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkM2qpDAQhZ8m7pT8mKiLLAbEXc92llImpYY2icRkmnn7wb403O1d1jkfB77685gf4A4Xtt_gUae8zumad0zortcO2QVE-y-WHEuwmGZOuaqprHl7c6yy2hoLzFSoWdcNSggmumrXbDXDyuSwUGkW1beUD1Qi7zvsOxisrZy-p6jkLWsFZ6qRfDU9R6uokQMMlrQUDky5SXiW5XAGQobrucZksDHRV4fecz4vIn4RPhE-XWhKwgYC2phvgvApPhFX9GgdbCmW8478Vucdaxtjqv1Sn_EEIqaS_XzFkgwSMX5nCFd3d28UT8T45r8yA_4EtwUixo_Mp4khY8hEjCmvhCvwsbxPIauk7flyx-Eu1ZGWbh7c8RbKP3__X83_BwAA__8XQZXW)** _**" Join the good guys. Be a hero. Blow the whistle. Come to our side. We want to work with you."**_ [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkM2qpDAQhZ8m7pT8mKiLLAbEXc92llImpYY2icRkmnn7wb403O1d1jkfB77685gf4A4Xtt_gUae8zumad0zortcO2QVE-y-WHEuwmGZOuaqprHl7c6yy2hoLzFSoWdcNSggmumrXbDXDyuSwUGkW1beUD1Qi7zvsOxisrZy-p6jkLWsFZ6qRfDU9R6uokQMMlrQUDky5SXiW5XAGQobrucZksDHRV4fecz4vIn4RPhE-XWhKwgYC2phvgvApPhFX9GgdbCmW8478Vucdaxtjqv1Sn_EEIqaS_XzFkgwSMX5nCFd3d28UT8T45r8yA_4EtwUixo_Mp4khY8hEjCmvhCvwsbxPIauk7flyx-Eu1ZGWbh7c8RbKP3__X83_BwAA__8XQZXW) [▶ WATCH THE CONFRONTATION AND CHIP IN $50](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkLGOtCAUhZ8GOw0C4lhQ_Imxm7_d0lzhomQEDMJO9u03zmaSbbe853w5yXc_7vMd3O7C-h88qpTtnM55w4TufG6QXUA0X7HkWILBNDPKZE27momLayujjDbQ6gpV2_eD5LzlfbWpwVp7EwIWKenCBWMdpe3S38B2AqSmlVPXFO2YaAVnrWw6ZvWNoZFUdwMMhggKO6bcJDzKsjsNIcP5sDFpbHT01a62nI-T8H-ETYRNJ-qSsIGAJuaLIGyKD0SLHo2DNcVyXJFf67xhbWJMtV_qIx5A-FSyn89YkkbCx98MYfLqro3iCR9f_E-mwR_g1kD4-JZ5NzFkDJnwMWVLmAQfy-vsaJWUOZ5u390peyLo6sHtL6H89_d_KvYdAAD___a8lbk) I want to tell you about the part of our work that almost no one sees. Everyone sees the videos -- the hidden-camera footage, the viral clips, the moment a powerful person gets caught. But the video is the last ten percent of what we do. It is the tip of an iceberg that costs a fortune and takes months to build. Behind every clip you have ever watched from us is a process most people can't imagine. Citizen journalists trained and sent undercover for weeks at a time. Encrypted equipment so footage can't be lost or seized. Lawyers reviewing every second before we publish. Security details -- because this work is genuinely dangerous, and people have threatened our lives for doing it. And then there is the part that actually defines us: we show up. In person. At the door. [▶ DONATE $100 TO FUND THE WHOLE PROCESS -- NOT JUST THE CAMERA](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkLGOqzAQRb_GdCCPDTgpXDwJ0eW1W6KJPYAVbCNjb7R_vyKrSNtuOfceXenMx226odtcWP6jJ53yPKVjWimRO54rZheI7FcsOZZgKU2Ci77mXS3ak4PKamssgqlIg1LXXkqQqlo18rnrRKfUrEBdWrCAFhAsEHFAoMrpc4p3ooVWCuibTszmIsj23HRXvFrWctwo5SbRXu6bMxgyHo85JkONib7a9JrzfjD5j4mRifEgUxI1GMjGfBJMjPFBNJMn63BJsexn5Jc6r1TbGFPt7_Ued2RyLNlPRyzJEJPDb4aJ_uzOjeKZHF78T2bQ7-iWwOTwlnk3MWQKmckh5ZmJHn0srxM4r5K2-9Ntmzt6xVq-eHTbyyj__f-fWnwHAAD__6cWlgk) Here is what I need you to understand. When I knock on that door, I am not there to destroy someone. I am there to give them a chance to do the right thing -- to turn, to become a whistleblower instead of a defendant. Because the truth is always better served by someone who decides to tell it than by someone we corner. That is the standard we hold ourselves to: expose the wrongdoing, yes -- but always offer the person a road back to the right side. People ask me all the time: James, how do you actually do it? How do you get people to talk? How do you find the nerve to walk up and knock on that door? The honest answer is that it takes everything. It takes journalists willing to risk themselves. And it happened because we did the slow, expensive, unglamorous work, **[all the way down to the knock on the door.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkM2qpDAQhZ8m7pT8mKiLLAbEXc92llImpYY2icRkmnn7wb403O1d1jkfB77685gf4A4Xtt_gUae8zumad0zortcO2QVE-y-WHEuwmGZOuaqprHl7c6yy2hoLzFSoWdcNSggmumrXbDXDyuSwUGkW1beUD1Qi7zvsOxisrZy-p6jkLWsFZ6qRfDU9R6uokQMMlrQUDky5SXiW5XAGQobrucZksDHRV4fecz4vIn4RPhE-XWhKwgYC2phvgvApPhFX9GgdbCmW8478Vucdaxtjqv1Sn_EEIqaS_XzFkgwSMX5nCFd3d28UT8T45r8yA_4EtwUixo_Mp4khY8hEjCmvhCvwsbxPIauk7flyx-Eu1ZGWbh7c8RbKP3__X83_BwAA__8XQZXW)** That is what your donations buy. The story was already out. The footage already spoke for itself. I could have stayed home and let the headlines do the work. But that is not how we do this. So I knocked. She opened the door. And instead of gloating, instead of a "gotcha," " Join the good guys. Be a hero. Blow the whistle. Come to our side. We want to work with you." I want to tell you about the part of our work that almost no one sees. Everyone sees the videos -- the hidden-camera footage, the viral clips, the moment a powerful person gets caught. Behind every clip you have ever watched from us is a process most people can't imagine. Citizen journalists trained and sent undercover for weeks at a time. Encrypted equipment so footage can't be lost or seized. Lawyers reviewing every second before we publish. clean_body: They looked like ordinary people The men arrested included a teacher, a cruise ship worker... and even a Santa Claus | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend, Most people think child traffickers look evil. They don't. Sometimes they look like a teacher. Sometimes they look like a cruise ship worker smiling at families on vacation. Sometimes they even dress like Santa Claus. That is the terrifying truth America is waking up to. And sadly, the news today reminds us why this mission matters so much. Disney cruise ship staffers among 28 arrested in massive child pornography operation. Well-known Santa Claus among 19 arrested in child predator sting. High School math teacher among 89 arrested in human trafficking operation. Three different stories. Three different places. But all convey one chilling truth ties them all together: The people who prey on children are hiding in plain sight. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am the producer of Sound of Freedom and founder of the Sound of Freedom Foundation. Years ago, after hearing firsthand stories about trafficked children, my life changed forever. What I learned broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold like products. And most people had no idea this darkness existed. Thart's why I helped create the Sound of Freedom film. Not for fame. Not for Hollywood. But because I believed people needed to see the truth. Many people told us the movie would fail. Studios rejected it. Doors closed. But I could not stay silent. A bombshell
report reveals Chief Justice John Roberts helped build the Supreme Court’s
“shadow docket” — a backdoor process for major rulings with no full
briefing, no arguments, and often no explanation.

What started as a rarely used emergency tool has been transformed into a
quiet pipeline for reshaping the law out of public view.

And under Trump, it’s been weaponized.

When Trump gets blocked in lower courts for breaking the law or pushing
unconstitutional policies, he runs straight to the Supreme Court demanding
an “emergency” order.

And this Court delivers:

30+ requests.
~80% success rate.

These are supposed to be temporary rulings. They’re not.

Immigrants lose protections. Civil servants get pushed out. Limits on
presidential power disappear all through unsigned, late-night orders with
no explanation.

Roberts set this precedent. Now it’s the playbook.

The bottom line is: this Court is operating without transparency,
accountability, or the restraint our democracy demands — and it won’t
change on its own.

Demand Justice PAC is exposing these abuses and building public and
political pressure needed to force reform — from ethics rules to
structural changes that rein in this out-of-control Court. But that
pressure only works if we can scale it.

Eduardo Verastegui is sounding the alarm to protect vulnerable children from trafficking. Will you join the fight?

| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend, A few weeks ago, I stood on a stage to receive the Catholic Champion Award. It was a humbling moment.
---
But as I held that award in my hands, I was not thinking about Hollywood. I was thinking about the children. And the millions of people who have joined this fight to protect them. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am a producer, actor, and founder of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**.
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=7d90da0b23a94730a3d7e5b6ecd050ff&_e=3fbXO1Q8i59OJcrFR6ETwOOgLqGkgw2_N761UJRDt3JyOKRj_eNwXUwb9BSsBQs6j5YBN9oNlThs1SCyIZqtfWicPrzXHtHbo_mGmVGEmycfg4OncLxWb6yNpy9e1IRljs4k2A3NfXDrkGvGZIP8DhadtSXwZo0imicaxY6dSgRE6DDtV3Z8Rk75CY-1kLIPOaGIQnTHes0P7FRmb2F7QU3_ePli7fTXVizzqzLgieK_y-pvYMz5gIYCstuvd7fQZpZlhlRa-V7vIwZt4U55K2MM4pvdb9-xaMK2PJHY6Z30t7J3Ing28HjSHnnHws41TQ2QjKSevHwlFQ-nJHowGD2XumOej1UaDmUun_dMLCvQaW8eVgm34Imek0iQFO7ZjfU8n6R2yxJTlA6f6Yl4llX_btOiPIaQRrGjxHCaDjNIABGSjAd7dKhAm8a-lh-vzfhr2ReT2KJR3W_DlBag1QgWVQxOUwOd5ViH3YGuaXVF1bTW64wp4EuS6dQH8PSseZUkHiSqkRu9rZ48o5Youh85-3EXsPyEjMuZnLv6GYow4noScNWhY20LxOdMYdziUT6wncutcCTyTQULKWoUGjFh-0LXiT92qn2g3GOv0xaXC5XvIEdwitzrlGwU-M6RISdOX0ktcUGWEbBdXKshYw%3D%3D)
---
Years ago, after hearing firsthand stories about children trapped in trafficking, my life changed forever. **What I learned broke my heart. **Children were being bought and sold for profit.
Families were being destroyed.

And most people had no idea this evil even existed.
---
[ Protect God’s Children. Give Now.](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=7d90da0b23a94730a3d7e5b6ecd050ff&_e=3fbXO1Q8i59OJcrFR6ETwOOgLqGkgw2_N761UJRDt3JyOKRj_eNwXUwb9BSsBQs6j5YBN9oNlThs1SCyIZqtfWicPrzXHtHbo_mGmVGEmycfg4OncLxWb6yNpy9e1IRljs4k2A3NfXDrkGvGZIP8DhadtSXwZo0imicaxY6dSgRE6DDtV3Z8Rk75CY-1kLIPOaGIQnTHes0P7FRmb2F7QU3_ePli7fTXVizzqzLgieJBBx5i7wV_0aI5BaMw644UCnFM3DIYKhn1iYUY5d4Cx0ybh7UBZwqKxeJTNpcBw2QaAeQydshv8nZBuLQEVSN56pMgYEs8IVr0GRvsJoFYbfph1WRxSyFYmxse_1aruf8aD-bIeK8Y4swfPSk6tmwSRUAlG0B9vsF88m4UrN182YfAp-jT_u2IKJUtU_L3bLrWp_hK5-_HXmFiubRMh7PLTnmzgfZMr6mwHnIAvDnot9e4rgPH1OBsuZmy8DNN5FIHHTkHJcLIyz309a8RnkvQXAT8LJGGPYxVBYaevK2vPlSZrd12tNhNBLwuuMxm4i1SGQjWS1yRFW3wlZ6iWDyliL4n7QTxmdyzXTcGWB51Hvwe2fUxL8Km0-373_9qy8y5Z90eL7DkUFB0NVDxPj7vQ6sR76G23-VUhkHq4xfBdg%3D%3D)
---
That is why I helped produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame. **
**Not for awards. **But because I believed people needed to see the truth. For years, many in Hollywood said the movie would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But we refused.** Because when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.
---
[ Protect God’s Children. Give Now.](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=7d90da0b23a94730a3d7e5b6ecd050ff&_e=3fbXO1Q8i59OJcrFR6ETwOOgLqGkgw2_N761UJRDt3JyOKRj_eNwXUwb9BSsBQs6j5YBN9oNlThs1SCyIZqtfWicPrzXHtHbo_mGmVGEmycfg4OncLxWb6yNpy9e1IRljs4k2A3NfXDrkGvGZIP8DhadtSXwZo0imicaxY6dSgRE6DDtV3Z8Rk75CY-1kLIPOaGIQnTHes0P7FRmb2F7QU3_ePli7fTXVizzqzLgieLklT1J1KWBRzNOv97mqLGkGPxSmK8mPU8cXz01TL1mhkE-I1ZYacs3vNp-aIHsktFhdJk1rnH5Ygvd3HMc0xgkcWZVVlpjyBA79PaCfZHyvJzq0lWzdiqjxKjb9ZEbtlT2PR_LgLoFcYgZgM86VhUNEwd_LS7NDpx5qj8PdrKU66cZcVGPQ5eeRp9nWMZXmBEABY738V8URM0HU-dcXZHLOBUFzGZWg7dX07A_jT50fA2iSeIoEThXlp83E_sYnpSJHGQRssHCYiLcMUVFXaoyngBDBhaDI6K6WXSG283f-en_WFnYpGPUfVmfWYhAw9NbG9BeqdcLPuzQe1DoVpAOUSjU3gVhPD95iM_mWGnBWufsCRyjFYgqMAB0uvd-hnqg4dzx2RxY1y45Z-ZQ04tXzKwk9XcKFnQAUrQBZtdjEA%3D%3D)
---
Today, the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** continues that mission beyond the movie screen. Earlier this month, **the Supreme Court put a dangerous lower court decision on hold** —one that could have severely restricted access to Mifepristone, a medication that has been used safely for more than 20 years in abortion care.

_That's good news._

For a lot of people, medication abortion is the only way they're able to access the care they need. But the fact is, this case is still moving through the courts. And the people trying to make abortion harder to access have not stopped, and won't until they get their way.

All we've seen since _Roe_ was overturned is extremist politicians and judges trying to take more and more control over deeply personal healthcare decisions. We've seen them try to make care harder to reach, even when it's safe, legal, and desperately needed. **People in Missouri know what happens when politicians interfere with reproductive healthcare, because we've lived through it more than once.**

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132006802/623064614/57398372?refcode=em26_260522_resend_fndd_gq_act___AB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260522_resend_fndd_gq_act___AB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=ea9a3a6e-8557-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZWE5YTNhNmUtODU1Ny1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=GK3MJFGmwAPSC7N3AiRq2rMCZoQP8acGVzn3K3Mg0g4=) Peter,

I sat down with Ali Vitali at MS NOW and said something I want to say to you directly:

This election for Democrats isn't a need-to-win. It's an absolute _have_ -to-win.

I meant every word of it.

We have 36 governor's races on the ballot this November. Thirty-six. And I believe that we can win in places people have written off. Iowa. Ohio. States that have drifted red but where the collision of Trump's tariffs, rising prices, and a healthcare system that's being hollowed out has people looking for something different.

Because here's what I've learned from winning three times in a state that went for Donald Trump by 30 points: people don't vote for a party. They vote for someone they trust to make their life better. Someone who can tell them not just what they're going to do, but why – what actually drives them to do this work.

Voters are craving authenticity right now. They want results and they want receipts.

And Democratic governors deliver. We create good jobs. We expand healthcare. We keep our promises. And right now, we are the most important line of defense against an administration that has absolutely no solutions for the families who are stretched thin at the end of every month.

When I talked about Ohio's Amy Acton and Iowa's Rob Sand, I wasn't just talking about two candidates. I was talking about what it looks like when we go on offense. When we compete everywhere. When we refuse to concede any state and any voter before the campaign even starts.

If we win those governor's mansions in Iowa and Ohio, we don't just help the people of those states. We build a map for the future that doesn't depend on five states and zero margin of error.

But none of this happens without resources.

Thank you,

* * *
Unity is the fruit of shared unifying moments.
Society does not achieve "unity" like it purchases a pie. Individuals participate in moments, humbly, removing oneself and one's personal agenda, and that fosters unity. Any calls for "unity" are hollow if those folks are incapable of joining in and defending unifying moments. "We need to come together" is irreconcilable with kneeling at the national anthem. Unity demands unifying moments.
Memorial Day is a unifying moment because at its core is that humility required to foster unity. Memorial Day is not about us, not in the slightest sense. Even the most powerful person on the planet is humbled by the solider who died in our nation's defense. Even the most decorated Marine alive takes a back seat to the deceased navy corpsman. We stand and honor those who gave it all.
Memorial Day is the ultimate unifying moment because the individual steps aside to celebrate and honor those who cannot take the microphone and talk about themselves like a crappy best man toast. The dead cannot accept praise, cannot blush from embarrassment, cannot say "thank you" and wave to the crowds. We celebrate those incapable of acknowledging it, and that humbles us.
We need humility to have unifying moments to foster unity.
The Department of Interior, at President Trump's orders, has begun a massive undertaking throughout Washington, DC to make the nation's capital safe and beautiful especially as we approach our 250th Anniversary.
This is a unifying moment.
