* * *
* * *
The Tidal Basin around the Jefferson Memorial, home to the famed cherry blossoms, was crumbling. The 2000-foot-long reflecting pools before the Lincoln Memorial were leaking and full of garbage and algae. Meridian Hill Park in north of the White House was a gathering place for crackheads and its large cascading fountain hadn't worked in nearly a decade. Lafeyette Square in front of the White House has not had working fountains since the Bush Administration. Columbus Fountain outside of Union Station hasn't been operable since the Carter Administration.
Missed opportunities to unite us.
All of this is being reversed. Sixteen months after his inauguration, President Trump has managed to fix decades of neglect, disrepair, disfunction, dilapidation in our nation's capital.
Why? Because they are places which foster unity. One cannot stand before the grandeur of the Columbus Fountain or the easily overlooked statue of Brigadier General Thaddeus Kościuszko without absenting one's self. They are physical reminders of another: stone, bronze, mortar, solid putting you in your place, forcing you to accept the greatness of someone else.
Washington, DC with its diagonal grand boulevards intersecting the grid, has hundreds of little areas with fountains, statutes, memorials all getting proper attention. Just a few days ago the Parks Department unveiled the renovated memorial to General Philip Sheridan (a Union General whose scorched earth tactics were so brutal that they pale in comparison to some Confederates Generals whose statutes leftists tore down a few years ago... but history is told by the victors and I'll avoid the comically oxymoronic tangent for another article...) designed by the same sculptor of Mount Rushmore where fountains had not worked since the Ford Administration. It is now restored and water again flows.
The President reopened a place where people remove themselves. A unifying place. Creating unity.
Working fountains, proper benches, decent lighting, fixed signage, flowers and trees, beauty itself, these are all unifying. It is why the left attacks them. Why, in their rage, they destroy what is not theirs. Why, in their hatred, they deface that which celebrates others. Why, in their own ego-driven administration, they diverted resource from that which creates unity like parks and memorials, to that which pushes their own agenda.
The Obama Department of Interior spent tens of millions rewriting all the signs at our national parks to emphasize climate change while he allowed the park outside the White House to crumble and serve prostitutes and drug dealers. Yes, Obama was looking for a form of unity around his vision, but not the nation.
Parks. Fountains. Memorials. Memorial Day itself. They transcend us, time and space, they force us to absent ourselves, to put someone or something else in the center even if that center is a small space is a tiny corner of a busy street.
We must fiercely defend unifying moments. The flag. The national anthem. The nation's capital and its many memorials, squares, statues, plinths, squares, and fountains. Memorial Day. The memory of others. The sacrifice of others.
Nothing about the self. America first through tangibly lived, shared, unifying places and moments. America first indeed.
**Honor and courage.**

Even the most powerful person on the planet is humbled by the solider who died in our nation's defense. Even the most decorated Marine alive takes a back seat to the deceased navy corpsman. We stand and honor those who gave it all. Memorial Day is the ultimate unifying moment because the individual steps aside to celebrate and honor those who cannot take the microphone and talk about themselves like a crappy best man toast. The dead cannot accept praise, cannot blush from embarrassment, cannot say "thank you" and wave to the crowds. We celebrate those incapable of acknowledging it, and that humbles us. We need humility to have unifying moments to foster unity. The Department of Interior, at President Trump's orders, has begun a massive undertaking throughout Washington, DC to make the nation's capital safe and beautiful especially as we approach our 250th Anniversary. This is a unifying moment. Sponsored by | | ---|---|--- The Tidal Basin around the Jefferson Memorial, home to the famed cherry blossoms, was crumbling. The 2000-foot-long reflecting pools before the Lincoln Memorial were leaking and full of garbage and algae. Meridian Hill Park in north of the White House was a gathering place for crackheads and its large cascading fountain hadn't worked in nearly a decade. Lafeyette Square in front of the White House has not had working fountains since the Bush Administration. Columbus Fountain outside of Union Station hasn't been operable since the Carter Administration. Missed opportunities to unite us. All of this is being reversed. Sixteen months after his inauguration, President Trump has managed to fix decades of neglect, disrepair, disfunction, dilapidation in our nation's capital. Why? Because they are places which foster unity. One cannot stand before the grandeur of the Columbus Fountain or the easily overlooked statue of Brigadier General Thaddeus Kościuszko without absenting one's self. They are physical reminders of another: stone, bronze, mortar, solid putting you in your place, forcing you to accept the greatness of someone else. Washington, DC with its diagonal grand boulevards intersecting the grid, has hundreds of little areas with fountains, statutes, memorials all getting proper attention. Just a few days ago the Parks Department unveiled the renovated memorial to General Philip Sheridan (a Union General whose scorched earth tactics were so brutal that they pale in comparison to some Confederates Generals whose statutes leftists tore down a few years ago... but history is told by the victors and I'll avoid the comically oxymoronic tangent for another article...) designed by the same sculptor of Mount Rushmore where fountains had not worked since the Ford Administration. It is now restored and water again flows. The President reopened a place where people remove themselves. A unifying place. Creating unity. Working fountains, proper benches, decent lighting, fixed signage, flowers and trees, beauty itself, these are all unifying. It is why the left attacks them. Why, in their rage, they destroy what is not theirs. Why, in their hatred, they deface that which celebrates others. Why, in their own ego-driven administration, they diverted resource from that which creates unity like parks and memorials, to that which pushes their own agenda. The Obama Department of Interior spent tens of millions rewriting all the signs at our national parks to emphasize climate change while he allowed the park outside the White House to crumble and serve prostitutes and drug dealers. Yes, Obama was looking for a form of unity around his vision, but not the nation. Parks. Fountains. Memorials. Memorial Day itself. They transcend us, time and space, they force us to absent ourselves, to put someone or something else in the center even if that center is a small space is a tiny corner of a busy street. We must fiercely defend unifying moments. The flag. The national anthem. The nation's capital and its many memorials, squares, statues, plinths, squares, and fountains. Memorial Day. The memory of others. The sacrifice of others. Nothing about the self. America first through tangibly lived, shared, unifying places and moments. America first indeed. Honor and courage. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

_**by Cliff Schecter**_
Always remember, folks: _tequila is cheaper than therapy._
Former Congressman Joe Walsh and I also had a great conversation on this edition of Tequila Talk! We covered:
* Trump actually said he got a "kick out of" the fact only 13 U.S. soldiers have died in Iran. We both, like any normal humans, are not surprised anymore, but still horrified by his sociopathy and malignant narcissism. Those are 13 soldiers who died for a war Trump's given a dozen explanations for fighting. 13 soldiers whose moms, dads, kids, wives, husbands, and close friends _will never see them again_. To that bloated-vat-of-corn-syrup-come-to-life, it's just about ego. Like everything.
To me it was a reminder of a line by William Munny in _Unforgiven, "It's a hell of a thing killin' a man. Take away all he's got and all he's ever gonna have. _Donald Trump took away all these 13 men and women were ever gonna have. For nothing. For an illegal war where he's getting his arse kicked [because he's God's perfect idiot](https://substack.com/redirect/477c2821-df82-4953-a7cc-60b3202efecc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Repulsive. We had more to say. Watch the video.

[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=198754501&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk4NzU0NTAxLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzk2Mzc4NjUsImV4cCI6MTc4MjIyOTg2NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.DtQ9QDEtvo6jKYQK6W5_CBALre6uZWzl0LdFKEHG6pk)
* We also talked about Trump's slush fund, which pretty clearly seems like a way to pay off his shock troops to help him try to steal the 2026 election. I liked how Chris Van Hollen took it to Trump's stump AG, Todd Blanche, on whether the funds would go to anyone who attacked Capitol Hill police on Jan 6th. Joe had a different take. That the message should be much more straightforward. I think he makes a pretty good point. Check it out in the video!
* [Rep. Thomas Massie lost in a GOP primary in Kentucky. After Trump opposed him](https://substack.com/redirect/2e61fea0-2de6-485c-a221-09f9ceb7cb0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), recruited a primary opponent, got record-breaking ad spending to go against him. All because he stood up to Trump to demand the Epstein files' release and opposed the war in Iran. Joe thinks Massie's loss is a "huge win" for Trump. I think just the opposite. Here's Joe below. _I tell you why in the video._

In a as little as 60 minutes! A great feel good story. There's more to it. Watch our discussion!

* Finally our funny of the week. If you see strange poop on your roof that didn't come from a bird, do yourself a favor--_Don 't Go Up To The Roof To See What It Is._
* [Jared Polis. I'm still enraged at the Democratic Governor for commuting the sentence of Trump's election attacker, Tina Peters. The Mesa County, CO elections official ](https://substack.com/redirect/384d2fd5-21fb-4354-901c-9817c3e76ea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[who broke into election software and leaked the contents publicly](https://substack.com/redirect/384d2fd5-21fb-4354-901c-9817c3e76ea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_. In the process, Polis overruled Democrats who thought the idea was nuts (CO Attorney General, Secretary of State, U.S. Senators), Republicans who thought the idea was nuts (Mesa County District Attorney and Clerk of Courts), and non-partisan folks doing their jobs (_a jury of her peers who found her guilty, the clemency board who said not to do it, an appellate court reviewing her sentence_). Polis has incentivized more attacks on our elections in 2026 by Trumpers.
_The billionaire-run networks applaud Polis.[He's a tech bro worth $300MM--like them](https://substack.com/redirect/384d2fd5-21fb-4354-901c-9817c3e76ea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)! I'm the daughter of Hmong refugees.

My parents fled the CIA's secret war in Laos and came to California with the hope that their children might have opportunities they never had.

I grew up in South Sacramento as the oldest of 16 kids.
Responsibility wasn't something I learned later in life — it was every day. I helped raise my siblings. I translated for my parents. I showed up when my community needed me.

When schools in my neighborhood were threatened with closure, I helped organize parents and co-founded _Hmong Innovating Politics_ so families like mine would have a voice.

When immigrant families were being terrorized during the first Trump administration, I championed **California's first Safe Haven Resolution** as a School Board member — making sure our schools remained places of safety regardless of immigration status.

**When something isn't right, I don't sit quietly and hope it changes. I step up. That's why I'm running for Congress.**

Families across CA-07 are being squeezed by the cost of living while our tax dollars get spent on endless wars. Too often Washington listens to corporate PACs and defense contractors instead of the communities they're supposed to serve.

I'm running to change that — and that's why I've committed to never taking corporate PAC money or a dime from AIPAC.

# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41421%2E3422442%2EsPQbOc)
Peter,
There’s a lot of candidates in this race with talking points about affordability.
**But Californians don’t need another politician handing out bumper-sticker promises. They need someone willing to break out the whiteboard and show the math.**
I’m running for governor because working families are getting crushed while giant corporations and wealthy special interests keep stacking the system in their favor.
Rent is too high. Child care is too expensive. Student debt follows people for decades. And meanwhile, the biggest corporations are finding loopholes to avoid paying what they owe.
**Unlike my opponents, I have a _real_ plan.**
My plan starts with making the biggest, most profitable corporations finally pay their fair share so we can actually lower costs for working people. That means tuition-free public college, lower costs for families, and eliminating state income taxes for Californians making under $100,000 a year.
_That’s how you make California affordable again—with real plans that pencil out._
And here’s another difference in this race: I’m not taking corporate PAC money. I’m not funded by Big Oil executives and I’m not writing my own campaign million dollar checks.
This campaign is powered by grassroots supporters chipping in what they can because they’re tired of watching politicians protect a system that works great for corporations and leaves everyone else behind.
**The primary is nine days away, and I need your help to make sure our message reaches all undecided voters across the state before they cast their ballots.**
**[If you’re ready for a governor who will actually take on corporate greed and fight for working families, I’d be grateful if you chipped in $5 — or whatever makes sense for you today.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260524_1_ak.u_FZYv&refcode=em20260524-41421&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41421%2E3422442%2EsPQbOc)**

Thank you,
Katie

Friends, last month we secured a historic victory: a jury found Live Nation and Ticketmaster liable for harming fans, artists, and venues through years of illegal anticompetitive conduct, including overcharging for tickets.
Now, we're finishing the job.
I asked the court to break up Live Nation and Ticketmaster for good. Our order would require Live Nation to divest Ticketmaster and sell off its major concert venues across the country, dismantling the structure that allowed this monopoly to thrive in the first place.
We’re asking the court for this new order because a verdict alone isn’t enough. Live Nation was previously subject to behavioral remedies and ignored them, so we’re seeking structural remedies to ensure they can no longer hold this illegal, anti-competitive power over the market.
Live Nation got rich not because it was better — but because it broke the law.
Artists were hurt, fans were overcharged, and venues and rival promoters were squeezed out, all because one company was allowed to dominate every corner of the live music industry.
While the Trump administration has abandoned consumers in the middle of an affordability crisis, illegal monopolies like this one have only made things worse. It’s clear we can’t trust massive corporations like Live Nation to do the right thing for consumers, so we’re fighting back — and we’re winning.

This move strips nearly 2 million Tennesseans of the representation they deserve.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260524-1&t=1&akid=3514%2E587540%2ELgsHP8)
Peter,
Last week, I received official notice from Tennessee House Speaker Cameron Sexton that I had been **removed from all of my state House committee assignments — _alongside every other_ Tennessee House Democrat.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260524_1_justin.FsI6hi&refcode=em20260524-3514&amount=5&t=2&akid=3514%2E587540%2ELgsHP8)
This is one of the **_most troubling abuses of power_** in our state’s history.
Peter, this kind of retaliation only works if we let them intimidate us into silence. I won’t let it, but I’ll need your help to keep fighting. **[So if you’re able to, split $5 or more right now with our campaign and Leaders We Deserve to keep our grassroots Movement strong enough to defend ourselves and our communities from this authoritarian attack.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260524_1_justin.FsI6hi&refcode=em20260524-3514&amount=5&t=3&akid=3514%2E587540%2ELgsHP8)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260524_1_justin.FsI6hi&amount=5&refcode=em20260524-3514&t=4&akid=3514%2E587540%2ELgsHP8)**
If this sounds familiar, it should. Because this is what TN House Republicans do when they don’t like what you have to say.
More than three years ago, they expelled me after I protested on the House floor against their inaction on gun violence. They thought they could make an example of me for _refusing_ to be quiet while our communities were hurting.
_Now,_ they’re doing it all over again.
In early May, they pushed through rigged, racist maps designed to _eliminate_ TN-09’s identity as a majority-Black, Democratic district. TN House Democrats stood together and made it clear that we would not stand for this injustice.
So they retaliated.
Committee assignments aren’t ceremonial positions. They’re how state lawmakers do the day-to-day work of representing our communities — from hearing bills, shaping policy, and fighting for the needs of the People who sent us there.
But no matter what, they can’t strip away our voice, our courage, and our commitment to our People and neighborhoods. Civil rights icon and former Representative John Lewis taught us to make good trouble — necessary trouble.
With your support, we’ll keep doing just that, Peter.

Hey folks,
This one got personal.
**Adam Mockler** and I dug into the Trump family corruption machine, the surreal dynamic between Trump and Don Jr., and the broader rot that's eating away at our institutions in real time. We talked about loyalty, family, greed, and what happens when political power becomes a vehicle for personal enrichment.
We also got into the absurdity of Republicans pretending to own "family values" while Trump skips his own son's wedding, spends his nights posting about Stephen Colbert, and lets his family cash in across the globe.
**Here are some moments you don 't want to miss:**
* [**00:01:03**] We break down Trump skipping Don Jr.'s wedding -- and why the way he talks about his own kids says everything about who he is.
* [**00:05:17**] We get into the emotional side of the Trump family dynamic, the cycle of abuse and validation, and why power without love creates deeply broken people.
* [**00:09:12**] We unpack the "trickle-down corruption" inside Trumpworld -- foreign deals, crypto schemes, Pentagon contracts, and billion-dollar pay-to-play politics.
* [**00:13:40**] We talk about the Qatar jet controversy, national security risks, and why this level of corruption is unlike anything we've seen in modern American politics.
* [**00:16:51**] We shift into solutions: banning gerrymandering, overturning Citizens United, restoring institutional trust, and building a coalition strong enough to actually fight back.

At its core, this episode is about what kind of country we want to be. We can't normalize endless corruption, endless grifting, and endless cruelty just because we've become exhausted by the chaos. We need accountability. We need stronger institutions. And we need people willing to speak honestly about what's happening -- even when it's uncomfortable. If you value conversations like this, help us keep building them.

| | **It’s not too late to celebrate the Hodge High Holidays with us! Tomorrow, Friday, May 22, at 7:00 PM
** Tessa celebrated her 38th birthday on May 20. Then on May 22 the founder of NotStepping Back, Andrew Hodge, celebrates his birthday. Right in the middle of the birthdays is May 21—the perfect day for them to marry sixteen years ago, so come wish them happy birthdays and anniversary.

The Hodge High Holidays and Silent Auction event will be held at the locally owned,**El Torito Restaurant and Meat Market** in Hesperia, California. Please join Tessa and Andrew for delicious food, fun, and fundraising during the last critical push before the primaries! Use the QR code above or [RSVP at Act Blue at this link.](https://us.list-manage.com/m7U58kOjBC6?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c) Let’s celebrate love, birthdays, community, NotStepping Back, and the fight to flip CA-23.

body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1411%2E1086043%2E2FuRQj)
Hey Peter, it's Wes.
This email is about all that we've accomplished — because I think you deserve to know what your support has made possible. But to keep in the fight, I need your support -- **[so if you’re already on board, please, chip in today.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260524-1.SYjWA_&refcode=em-20260524-1&t=2&akid=1411%2E1086043%2E2FuRQj)**
Since I became Governor, here’s what we’ve done together, Peter:
➡️ We reduced homicides in Maryland -- to the lowest level in decades.
➡️ We raised teacher salaries and brought new businesses back at a rate we haven't seen since before the pandemic.
➡️ We lowered energy bills for families across the state by $200 million.
**That's not a promise. That's a record.**
But here's the hard truth: Maryland's fundraising laws meant I spent months governing — not fundraising. While Republican opponents raised money every single day of the year, we weren't legally allowed to.
That gap is real. And it's why I need you now.
**[Can you chip in $5 to help us protect everything we've built together? We’ll only win re-election with a strong grassroots movement, so I’m counting on your support.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260524-1.SYjWA_&refcode=em-20260524-1&t=3&akid=1411%2E1086043%2E2FuRQj)**

Thank you. I'm proud to have you in this fight.
Elevate,
Wes

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Some good news, some bad news
body:
Good news and bad news
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
I have some good news... and some bad news.
→ The good news is that the latest polls show we’re ahead of Greg Abbott.
→ The bad news is that Abbott is already trying to buy his way. At two separate events in Houston, he said it himself. He’s planning to spend **$25 million to turn Harris County red.**
That should tell you _everything_ you need to know about the state of the race right now. Abbott can feel the ground shifting, so he’s doing what he always does when Texans start demanding change. He’s calling in the big bucks.
I’ll be honest, Peter. That makes me nervous, because I’ve seen how quickly outside spending can try to drown out momentum and can be discouraging to voters who want to see real leadership change.
But here’s something I also know.
**Abbott can spend millions, but he can never match the power of Texans who are ready to vote for something better.** We don’t have to match him dollar for dollar. We just have to have the resources to stay on the air, keep organizing, and keep talking directly to voters in every corner of Texas.
That’s why we set a **$100,000 end-of-month fundraising goal by May 31.** If we hit it, we’ll be ready for the next wave of attacks, and we’ll keep building the campaign it takes to win.
**So I’m asking, Peter:** **[will you chip in $5 or anything you can right now to help my campaign fight back and hit our $100,000 goal?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260524_1_goal.DgBtWN&refcode=em20260524-1183&amount=5&t=1&akid=1183%2E299639%2EKxK8LT)**

Thank you,
Gina

name: Jen Kiggans
subject: Can I borrow you for a few minutes?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kiggans for Congress
body:
From Navy helicopter pilot to Congress
| Fellow American,
I know your inbox is probably overflowing right now with politicians begging for your hard-earned money using every scare tactic in the book.
I truly hate having to send messages like this, but I really appreciate your time!
My last message didn't get the response I was hoping for, and now I'm starting to feel like we're falling behind. We can't keep fighting if we don't have the resources to keep the lights on and pay my amazing staff.
Let me take a second to re-introduce myself: My name is Jen Kiggans.
I am a former Navy helicopter pilot. I flew H-46s and H-3s in the Persian Gulf. After my time in the military, I used my GI Bill benefits to go back to school and become a board-certified Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. I am married to a retired Navy F/A-18 pilot, and now I am a proud Navy Mom.

And that is exactly WHY I ran for Congress in 2022.
I knew that I needed to step up and do my part to make sure that my four kids inherit a GREAT America!
Against all odds, we flipped Virginia's 2nd District RED in one of the tightest, must-win races in the entire country. But elections have serious consequences and these radical Left Democrats are not going to give up without a fight.
Now, National Democrats and Left-leaning Super PACs are raking in millions to attack me and take back the House this year. They want to turn our great commonwealth into California AND my far-Left opponent JUST announced she raised over $1.75 MILLION in the first quarter alone.

Hello Fellow Patriot, I'd like to introduce myself.

My name is Jackie Mary Auringer, and I'm running for U.S. Congress because I am no longer willing to leave the future of my community in the hands of people I can't trust.

For too long, the voices of families in the Hudson Valley have been ignored or filtered through agendas, which don't reflect what life is really like here, especially as the cost of living continues to rise and families are stretched thinner every year.

**I am not bought by outside interests, nor am I driven by personal ambition.**

My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District.

My loyalty is to this community, its families, its future, and its strength.

Our nation is too divided, and it's holding us back.

I believe we can do better.

We can lead with purpose, bring people together, focus on real results, support families, and rebuild confidence in our leadership.

My focus is on advancing practical solutions that support families like mine, bolster local businesses, and strengthen our community as a whole.

[](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=dafdee69cce84a44bd27734537f9c096&_e=37yQxN5rTrkXzSSWvhmk3v4PGPUcpwhb0YxIMz9WrmR1WW8VfAXh1Gf-i2VcoejKTNRYMweKESaPv6l8Wt7GRx5Ab8VO7aq85hpAdbWsqFa6ZzlUZ8bmUhzDy2HmMhy5lX6t6fEJLB1MduXwG3Whd4x6FWffGOChcAImlLeZPDKXmIjtpJmTZRzZ9qF_ZcB1eFxhCvmwiMcivzdfpyJARJ_gTzxbaFBPUaSgOfbv-FdQ9Q8xx14ylLD4thqgI5vNdNnfnpgDjPm3-M9YM2aoIY4tATLeaCGlvikOGErV1rPWghs41EDBzBjhXa-jIKD3ymihv1GhW7IyJgF7YqVA8storoTY05mWkBarlPdjxaleaBXd-fniCSqgqXOnMukMxxZlCRq8_c015E9EvkBcCwZwWplMj8rc0PhQaUkBtVMH76XE1T_jKMn8drIvyrgnthEOfWXNYOYKZsMZcA-nGV-XwimqKnePMYAWLHVzhbP5IdOqeXdxny2omqQxOUpL13OSVM4Cu3-dXsPMVOo7cmfo5vU4GxlaEca-EpTtBIZNpd7tbcbFryT3mmdIEgHSnfkwzWtjQEqqgAe-goiUN1vxCTQ3N2qxqh13nwIzKy4PeYwI3RxC9kqpNlCv2yk4-hsoD3o7NwjnDVhzf2HMhwD9YZjF7MJTOhI1hzx17jsVgZ0eiCZfuxSZ2bqajcsI2owF6lBubNijs6U4WW0kgw%3D%3D)
I'm a proud Hudson Valley native. I was born and raised there and shaped by parents who dedicated their lives to serving it, my mother as a teacher and my father through his construction business.

**They taught me what matters: responsibility, accountability, and pride in where you come from.**

Growing up in that environment gave me a firsthand understanding of the importance of hard work, community involvement, and local pride. That perspective is what drives my commitment to ensuring the Hudson Valley is represented by someone who knows it, values it, and will always put it first.

[](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=dafdee69cce84a44bd27734537f9c096&_e=37yQxN5rTrkXzSSWvhmk3v4PGPUcpwhb0YxIMz9WrmR1WW8VfAXh1Gf-i2VcoejKTNRYMweKESaPv6l8Wt7GRx5Ab8VO7aq85hpAdbWsqFa6ZzlUZ8bmUhzDy2HmMhy5lX6t6fEJLB1MduXwG3Whd4x6FWffGOChcAImlLeZPDKXmIjtpJmTZRzZ9qF_ZcB1eFxhCvmwiMcivzdfpyJARJ_gTzxbaFBPUaSgOfbv-FdQ9Q8xx14ylLD4thqgI5vNp1eikiSBVzj2zVw2790UwCr9b9rTAbUyoyvTUf20zXWY3LyHmlAqU9JVsTH3YY2m5IWNDFmkXbvgv_u5nEJbALym6-6WyzXVMDgtL1F7DvcX7eNpQvitTC2L4IpLUayui_TzCJiCp8S91EFbg6htm3FUfllMqkYDdWP_EXzYEI5ezG1SGcH486KQrjOsw3dUqi9PiEqAylUczoxBpX0SPNzqiCZ96VGP32BWU7ZvG9x6JJIJTzI0wuf7E2wUTmQ-kjRsF-aaqCJlngnHVwaQITbVyJykSM5pg-RzK1d9VGNcVVjKbRCFwpY_8aAqsEOt-ZUKmbJcwV-eHWNLs91av1hqfAHTCl1D6yrBTxRl_4MtJAjxlNUphc7Z102Yyqp083r-rg-9s-6SdXMZzioJTGSm9wIxtu67Z8rn5SUOKZuWlP7Pe6VI65P64gm-oPNf4banZH8d3fmyhcPbxEE7AQ%3D%3D)
I believe that family is the foundation. This lens formed my values and the way I approach servant leadership. That means being a good neighbor and respecting others. The Hudson Valley shaped every part of who I am, and I am committed to protecting our way of life to ensure future generations can thrive in our community. Just like my family did.

**So, I'm humbly asking for your support before my first campaign deadline on May 31st as I embark on this mission to give my hometown the representation it's longed for.**

clean_body: My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District. | Hello Fellow Patriot, I'd like to introduce myself. My name is Jackie Mary Auringer, and I'm running for U.S. Congress because I am no longer willing to leave the future of my community in the hands of people I can't trust. For too long, the voices of families in the Hudson Valley have been ignored or filtered through agendas, which don't reflect what life is really like here, especially as the cost of living continues to rise and families are stretched thinner every year. I am not bought by outside interests, nor am I driven by personal ambition. My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District. My loyalty is to this community, its families, its future, and its strength. Our nation is too divided, and it's holding us back. I believe we can do better. We can lead with purpose, bring people together, focus on real results, support families, and rebuild confidence in our leadership. My focus is on advancing practical solutions that support families like mine, bolster local businesses, and strengthen our community as a whole. I'm a proud Hudson Valley native. I was born and raised there and shaped by parents who dedicated their lives to serving it, my mother as a teacher and my father through his construction business. They taught me what matters: responsibility, accountability, and pride in where you come from. Growing up in that environment gave me a firsthand understanding of the importance of hard work, community involvement, and local pride. That perspective is what drives my commitment to ensuring the Hudson Valley is represented by someone who knows it, values it, and will always put it first. I believe that family is the foundation. This lens formed my values and the way I approach servant leadership. That means being a good neighbor and respecting others. The Hudson Valley shaped every part of who I am, and I am committed to protecting our way of life to ensure future generations can thrive in our community. Just like my family did. So, I'm humbly asking for your support before my first campaign deadline on May 31st as I embark on this mission to give my hometown the representation it's longed for. I've got your back, Fellow Patriot. ---|---
Dear Patriot, I wrote this because I do not want this moment to pass quietly. You get a lot of campaign emails. I know that. Most of them are overly urgent and instantly forgettable.
| | ★ |
---|---|---
Deadlines. Buttons. Exclamation points. The usual performance. **This is not that.** I wrote you a real note because **June 2nd is almost here** , and after that, this race moves on with us or without us.
|
---
Please read what I wrote | [Read My Message](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4ODZ9AAwAAAAAAM-6LVNb0hJHABy0kYXz0HHUF1Ku_cOzNyoquSbV-QOi3xEPfc3mOTjNC_DJN-r1v1C9_ImO3zWy-fJDF4re9BFSh8Qejj2as-UBIw4B)

| There is no automatic Republican nominee in California. There is no second chance if we fall short. There is no clever explanation that will make up for failing to do everything possible while there was still time.
---
**That is the brutal, unavoidable fact.** And frankly, I do not want this to be the last serious message I send to Americans across the country about this campaign because Democrats managed to stop us before November. **That would be a bitter, ridiculous ending to a fight we can absolutely win.**
| Before the window closes Help me keep this campaign moving. | [Stand With Me](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ4ODZ9AAwAAAAAAM-6LVNcFqyVDfOpv1JZCTyDghsIfFwYBHhWshx96bn_Yfvp2Xuu2Onyq6vHCS1T0ux9pQw3N3AwKGTe953tOh-HU9puBqzsMERIYgv8)

So before you scroll past another campaign email, I want you to read the note I wrote. It explains exactly where this race stands, why Democrats want us buried before June 2nd, and why I believe they are terrified of facing us one-on-one in November. They should be.
|

_Steve Hilton_

Peter,
---
It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**

clean_body: This Memorial Day begins America’s 250th – join me It's Gary Sinise here. | | | | Peter, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Peter, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Peter, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. | | | | | | | | This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Peter, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. You may have heard that the South Carolina Supreme Court has overturned Alex Murdaugh's murder convictions — I have some thoughts.
If you haven’t been following the case (or watching the Netflix documentary series), here’s what you need to know:
Murdaugh is a wealthy, well-connected white attorney who was caught on video at the scene of his wife and son's murders. A jury of his peers convicted him, and a judge sentenced him to life in prison.
And now, he’s getting another trial.
Meanwhile, you and I both know that’s not what our justice system looks like for everyone else. Not for Black and brown Americans who are stopped, charged, convicted, and incarcerated at staggering rates for doing far less.
Not for immigrants swept up in ICE raids and held in detention facilities, unable to reach a lawyer.
And not for the countless voters whose fundamental rights are being eroded by a right-wing Supreme Court majority that’s clearly more interested in protecting power than delivering justice.
Just look at the total evisceration of the Voting Rights Act, delivered by SCOTUS last month: now, anyone challenging discriminatory maps must prove intentional discrimination, not just discriminatory effects. Just one hour after the ruling, the Florida House passed new, aggressively-gerrymandered maps. Other states are now following suit. Decades of progress undone in a single ruling.
And then in Virginia, the state Supreme Court actually threw out the results of the people's redistricting referendum — a direct rebuke of voters who stood up to Donald Trump and went to the ballot box to defend democracy and combat the GOP’s gerrymandering.
This is the Republican Party’s strategy: Use the courts to lock in their power before voters can step up to take it back.
Americans have been losing faith in our court system for years, and it’s no wonder why!
We need significant, structural reform to restore the legitimacy of our courts — before it’s too late.
I think everything should be on the table — like term limits for Supreme Court justices, so no president can shape the court for generations just by having lucky (or corrupt) timing. It could mean expanding the bench to 13 justices, or 15 justices with a rotational structure, all ideas that deserve to be discussed seriously and openly.
These are critical conversations we need to have as a country, because our court system has one set of rules for wealthy, white men clinging to power, and an entirely different set of rules for everyone else — and we can’t let it stay that way.
I want to know where you stand on this. If you support reforming the Supreme Court to restore its legitimacy and rebuild trust with the American people, will you add your name today to let me know? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/9gKeB5cP2kCdBsF-f6AY_A2]
ADD MY NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/9gKeB5cP2kCdBsF-f6AY_A2]
Justice should not depend on who you are, who you know, or which party appointed your judge. We deserve a court system that actually lives up to that promise.
–Sara

Trump and his MAGA allies are making it worse.
#
Peter,
Latinos are some of the hardest-working people in this country. But too many of our families are still being pushed further behind.
Here are some quick stats for you to know:
**Latino households hold about _22 cents_ in wealth for every _$1_ held by white households, and median Latino household wealth is roughly _$62,000_ , compared to _$284,000_ for white households.**
That gap is not an accident, Peter. This is a direct result of _decades_ of policy choices that made it harder to build stability, own a home, save for retirement, and get ahead.
And now, Trump and his MAGA allies are making it worse.
Trump ran on his economic promises to our communities, but instead, he’s ruined our economy. He’s too busy focused on building his ballroom, giving ICE a blank check, and using our tax dollars for his own benefit — **and it’s our families that pay the price.**

# [I want to know what keeps you up at night](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=198718948&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk4NzE4OTQ4LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzk2NDYwMjAsImV4cCI6MTc4MjIzODAyMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.DnxUftEMvL50RHPE5vNqIOpdAPCSHZHpOqqFEHhXjig)
### What do you think.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| May 24
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..hLRhScorJDVQ-QCUDUpc3K1qRz6TLJX0qEYbj9ExgJU?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/i-want-to-know-what-keeps-you-up?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Hi friends,
I love talking to people, especially Michiganders. I crack open a pop and chat until the cows come home.
But here's a little secret to being an effective politician: _Stop talking._
Truly. Michiganders know what Michigan needs better than anyone. I learned a long time ago that the first step to getting stuff done is always the same: **listen.**
That's why I'm reaching out with a simple request: **[Will you take one minute to fill out my 2026 Priorities Survey? We're collecting 1,000 responses before midnight tomorrow, and I'd be honored to hear from you directly.](https://substack.com/redirect/ca13ae1c-160f-4e3a-8eed-6d48fb93ecb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Take the survey](https://substack.com/redirect/ca13ae1c-160f-4e3a-8eed-6d48fb93ecb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Here 's why it matters:**
This is shaping up to be one of the most competitive Senate races in the country. Poll after poll shows I'm neck and neck with MAGA Republican Mike Rogers, and _The New York Times_ even recently named Michigan a key battleground in the fight for Senate control.
The stakes are high. That's why GOP billionaire megadonors are lining up behind Rogers, trying to buy this seat so they can rubber-stamp Trump's chaos agenda in the Senate.
So how do we fight back? **By building a grassroots campaign that listens, learns, and leads - in that order.**
We've already made so much progress:
✅ I introduced the **Stop Trump 's Abuse of Power Act** after Donald Trump abused his power and deployed the military against U.S. citizens.
✅ I led the charge to bring **semiconductor manufacturing back** to Michigan, creating good-paying jobs for our communities.
✅ I introduced the **No Tariffs on Groceries Act** to stop Trump's chaotic price hikes at the checkout line.
✅ I filed articles of impeachment against **RFK Jr.** for putting public health at risk and lying to Congress.
I'm proud of this work. Because it all came from listening to the _real_ concerns of _real_ people - and then taking action to fight for them.
So as we build a winning strategy for what will be a generation-defining election in Michigan, I want to make sure this campaign reflects _your_ priorities.
What's keeping you up at night? What change do you want to see? What matters most to you and your family? How can the government actually help you?
**[Will you please take a minute and let me know? It's a short survey, but it truly helps a ton.](https://substack.com/redirect/ca13ae1c-160f-4e3a-8eed-6d48fb93ecb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Take the survey](https://substack.com/redirect/ca13ae1c-160f-4e3a-8eed-6d48fb93ecb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is your campaign just as much as it's mine. And together, we're going to make history.
I'm so glad you're here.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
######
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c73f5ff5-29a0-4f3c-9a5b-ef0e3fbc1b41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Beneath the bustling streets of America's major cities lies a hidden world that most residents and visitors never see. From bustling commercial hubs to forgotten historical passageways, these subterranean networks reveal fascinating stories of urban ingenuity, historical necessity, and modern adaptation.

Seattle Underground, Washington stands as perhaps America's most famous subterranean city. Created after the devastating Great Fire of 1889, Seattle rebuilt by elevating its streets approximately 12 feet above the original ground level. The original sidewalks and storefronts became underground passages, now offering guided tours through this accidental catacomb of forgotten storefronts and architectural remnants.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=199087128&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk5MDg3MTI4LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzk2NDYxMTMsImV4cCI6MTc4MjIzODExMywiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.IQYkjoY_KNWm2ZBQP6nTg2zD_E6Fv8f1GBqYKLCVjv8)
Beneath Denver International Airport (DIA) lies an expansive "underground city" spanning over a million square feet, featuring 7,000-foot tunnels used for luggage transport via automated systems and service vehicle traffic. This functional subterranean area, sometimes patrolled by police, also includes newer, massive tunnels for collecting and recycling deicing fluid.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9fd7739c-5f84-4a73-94ca-04715c9c54ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
SubTropolis, Kansas City, Missouri represents the commercial evolution of underground living. Built into a former limestone mine, this sprawling 55-million-square-foot business complex maintains a constant 68-degree temperature year-round. Today, it houses numerous companies storing goods and operating businesses in a subterranean environment that offers both climate control and security.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.jnb7K0gGFQNfNDif-wcDTz6TKNwZwt5Z60AjUeNn_0Y?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199087128)
Underneath Disney World's Magic Kingdom lies the 'Utilidors" (Unitlity Corridos), a massive 9-acre network of tunnels acting as an underground city for cast members. Built at ground level to avoid Florida's high water table, these tunnels allow staff to move between lands, manage trash via vacuum tubes, access costume storage, and operate cafeterias, keeping all "backstage" logistics hidden from guests above.

Oklahoma City Underground demonstrates postmodern urban planning. Constructed in the 1970s to connect downtown buildings, this tunnel system stretches from the OG&E building to the Myriad Convention Center, offering climate-controlled walkways that protect pedestrians from the city's extreme weather.

Dallas Underground Tunnels, Texas emerged in the early 1970s with a similar purpose: connecting downtown buildings while beating the oppressive Texas heat. Originally featuring shops and restaurants, this network allowed office workers to navigate the city center without stepping outside.

Indianapolis Catacombs present a historical mystery. Located beneath the downtown City Market, these brick-vaulted tunnels served as Tomlinson Hall's basement. Though the original building burned, the underground catacombs remain, offering eerie tours through 19th-century construction.

Portland Shanghai Tunnels, Oregon carry darker historical significance. Legend claims these passages were used for shanghaiing--kidnapping people to serve on ships. Whether strictly factual or embellished, these tunnels beneath Chinatown remain fascinating attractions connecting buildings to the waterfront.

Crystal City Underground, Arlington, Virginia transformed a retail district during the Cold War. This network connects office buildings and shops beneath crystal towers, allowing workers to avoid winter weather and summer humidity entirely.

Las Vegas Drainage Tunnels, Nevada reveal modern adaptation. Originally built for flood control, these tunnels along the Las Vegas Wash have become unintended shelter for the unhoused population, showcasing how underground spaces serve different social purposes than originally intended.

Pittsburgh Tunnels, Pennsylvania extend beyond vehicle traffic. The Cathedral of Learning's Nationality Rooms and various downtown tunnels connect the hilly terrain, while Point State Park hides underground facilities beneath its surface.

Greenbrier Bunker, West Virginia represents governmental subterranean planning. This Cold War-era fallout shelter was built to house Congress in case of nuclear attack. The secret facility remained hidden for decades, only revealed in 1992, demonstrating how seriously America prepared for underground survival.

The [Vegas Loop](https://substack.com/redirect/17802b45-dbf5-4b93-bc7f-68ad5f086c96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is an underground transportation system built by Elon Musk's [The Boring Company](https://substack.com/redirect/0c6c06ed-f96d-4566-bbf6-58faf8a360fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Las Vegas, featuring Tesla vehicles driving in tunnels to transport passengers. Currently operating with over 2 miles of track and 8 stations, it aims for a 68-mile, 104-station network connecting the Convention Center, Strip, and Airport.

In January 2024, an illegal tunnel was discovered beneath the Chabad-Lubavitch World Headquarters at 770 Eastern Parkway in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, leading to a chaotic confrontation between worshippers and the New York City Police Department (NYPD).

The "tunnel" was actually an illegally excavated passageway, estimated at 60 feet long, 8 feet wide, and 5 feet tall, connecting the synagogue to an adjacent, empty apartment building. The tunnel was dug by a group of young men within the Hasidic community, often described as a "splinter sect" or "extremist students" associated with Chabad messianism. Members of this group, who believe that the late Lubavitcher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson is the Messiah and still alive, built the tunnel to "expand" the synagogue, citing a long-standing desire to grow the crowded sanctuary.

When leadership, which rejects this messianic view, sought to fill in the tunnel, these students staged a protest, leading to a brawl, vandalism, and the eventual arrival of the NYPD on January 8, 2024.

Nine to twelve individuals were initially arrested for actions including criminal mischief and reckless endangerment. By April 2024, several men were facing charges, with some entering plea deals to lesser charges, including probation and restitution for damages.

The illegally constructed tunnel caused structural damage, prompting the Department of Buildings to issue vacate orders for some adjacent buildings, including a former women's mikvah (ritual bath).

The tunnel was officially filled with cement by construction crews shortly after its discovery.

The incident resulted in viral, false, and antisemitic conspiracy theories online, with some users creating AI-generated imagery or falsely associating the space with trafficking or malicious acts.

The building remains a highly revered site in the Chabad-Lubavitch movement, and the leadership has condemned the actions of the group that dug the tunnel.

America's newest addition is underway. [The Boring Company](https://substack.com/redirect/1eccceac-7c3c-4a18-825f-6ad118d23ea9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), owned by Elon Musk, is constructing the "Music City Loop" in Nashville, a 25-mile underground transit tunnel connecting Nashville International Airport (BNA) to downtown and West End using Tesla vehicles. The project began tunneling this year with an initial 13-mile, privately funded phase projected to finish by 2027.

Not since the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, completed in 2010 and is the tallest building in the world, standing at a record-breaking 2,717 feet, has the "skyscraper" held our collective imaginations.

These hidden networks, where the sun does not shine, reveal that American cities have always worked in multiple dimensions--accommodating growth, escaping weather, and preparing for uncertain futures beneath their visible skylines.

Friend,

The primary is just 30 days away.

Getting here has taken a lot of hard work. Our team of volunteers has already knocked on 4,866 doors across the district to talk to our neighbors.

Most of this work isn’t glamorous. It is hours of picking up the phone, meeting voters where they are, and having real conversations about the issues that actually affect people's lives.

But that has always been Sarah’s way. She shows up for the parts of the job that don't make the headlines, and this campaign is no different.

We can’t afford to let up now. We need to keep this pace going every single day until the polls close.

Can you start a $10 recurring donation today to help us finish this campaign the right way? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-May2026-FR-30daysout?&recurring=auto&refcode=E29748-20260524-30daysMay-SL-2026Race&amount=10]

Donate ➔ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-May2026-FR-30daysout?&recurring=auto&refcode=E29748-20260524-30daysMay-SB-2026Race&amount=10]

A recurring gift is the best way to help us plan for this final push. It keeps our organizers out in the community and makes sure we have what we need to reach every undecided voter.

We’ve built something incredible together over the last few months. Now, we just have to see it through to the finish line.

Thanks for being on this team.

Team Elfreth

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. From Orange County to the Central Valley, from Inland Empire swing districts to competitive suburban communities, volunteers showed up ready to fight forward for California and for our democracy. = = = Here’s what Democrats accomplished this weekend: ➡️ Thousands of voter conversations across key battleground districts; ➡️ Phonebanks and canvasses focused on turning out Democratic voters for the June 2 Primary Election; ➡️ Literature distribution and voter outreach in multiple languages; ➡️ Volunteer recruitment and organizing efforts that will continue through Election Day and beyond. And here’s the most important part: This is only the beginning. Republicans know California will decide control of the U.S. House in 2026. That’s why MAGA Republicans and dark money groups are already pouring resources into protecting vulnerable GOP incumbents and attacking Democrats across the state. But this weekend proved something powerful: Democrats are organized, energized, and ready to fight back. Grassroots organizing is how we’ve flipped seats in the past. It’s how we passed Prop 50. And it’s how we will take back the House Majority. But organizing at this scale requires real, ongoing resources. = = = = = = = Thank you so much, \- The organizing team at CADEM HQ | | = Our Democratic leaders are working hard to make California a better place to live. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132016975/623095154/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImEwZjQwMDdiLTljNTctZjExMS04ZmNiLTAwMGQzYTE4OTA1YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=b_A7orm9CfPZLtIL8r1JQKgn8mPm4fgj-g8vse6Ud7M=&emci=bb6cc709-4e55-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&emdi=a0f4007b-9c57-f111-8fcb-000d3a18905c&ceid=8431045)

Peter, What Tennessee just did is a throwback to one of the ugliest chapters in American history. Just hours after the Supreme Court gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the state put its plan into motion. And eight days later, they had a new congressional map. Republicans in the state had erased Tennessee’s only Black opportunity district — creating a map in which all nine of the state’s districts were majority-white. Their actions directly aim to prevent the people of Memphis — one of the largest U.S. cities with a majority Black population — from being able to elect a representative of their choice. **Tennessee Republicans are not alone. ** **Louisiana** suspended an ongoing election to rip up their current map and eliminate a Black opportunity district. **Alabama, Mississippi, and South Carolina** are all making moves to follow in their footsteps. If there was any doubt that the protections of the Voting Rights Act are still essential today, the rushed actions of these southern states should put that to rest. **The Republican Party is waging an active campaign to reboot Jim Crow. ** It is brazen, it is shameless, it is wrong — and it must fail. History is playing out in front of our eyes, and it requires us to muster every ounce of energy we have to fight back. No one understands that better than me.
| **__A Letter from the Desk of Rep. Elise Stefanik__**
---
Peter,
---
President Trump has made it clear that he’ll do whatever it takes to WIN the midterms because he knows how vital our House Majority is to passing the America First agenda: _**“We must keep the Majority _at_ _all_ _costs_.”**_
---
No one understands that better than me.
---
Last year, I did what our country needed and withdrew my nomination to serve in President Trump’s cabinet to remain in the House and _protect_ our razor-thin Majority.
---
_And thank God I did. My vote was ultimately the tie-breaking vote to pass the President’s Big Beautiful Bill and grant tax cuts to millions of American families!_
---
For me, America First was never just a campaign slogan.
---
For every remaining minute that I have the honor to serve you in Congress, doing what’s right for our country will _**always**_ be my top priority.
---
**That’s why, even though I’m no longer running for reelection, I’m still committed to doing everything I can to help the President DEFEND his Majority.**
---
_Since I no longer need funds for my own campaign, I’ve decided the most effective way I can help is to use my grassroots donor network –**among the most powerful in the entire country** – to help America First Republicans WIN the key battleground races of the midterms. _
---
_After all the sacrifices I’ve made for our House Majority, you can rest assured that I’m going to spend every second I have left in Congress fighting to stop the Democrats from seizing control and DESTROYING everything we’ve fought so hard to accomplish._
---
But as we approach yet another critical fundraising deadline, I have no choice but to ask dedicated America First patriots like YOU to join me.
---

clean_body: No one understands that better than me. | A Letter from the Desk of Rep. Elise Stefanik Peter, President Trump has made it clear that he’ll do whatever it takes to WIN the midterms because he knows how vital our House Majority is to passing the America First agenda: “We must keep the Majority at all costs.” No one understands that better than me. Last year, I did what our country needed and withdrew my nomination to serve in President Trump’s cabinet to remain in the House and protect our razor-thin Majority. And thank God I did. My vote was ultimately the tie-breaking vote to pass the President’s Big Beautiful Bill and grant tax cuts to millions of American families! For me, America First was never just a campaign slogan. For every remaining minute that I have the honor to serve you in Congress, doing what’s right for our country will always be my top priority. That’s why, even though I’m no longer running for reelection, I’m still committed to doing everything I can to help the President DEFEND his Majority. Since I no longer need funds for my own campaign, I’ve decided the most effective way I can help is to use my grassroots donor network –among the most powerful in the entire country – to help America First Republicans WIN the key battleground races of the midterms. After all the sacrifices I’ve made for our House Majority, you can rest assured that I’m going to spend every second I have left in Congress fighting to stop the Democrats from seizing control and DESTROYING everything we’ve fought so hard to accomplish. But as we approach yet another critical fundraising deadline, I have no choice but to ask dedicated America First patriots like YOU to join me. Thank you and God Bless, Rep. |
Peter,
$1.6 billion.
The single largest political contribution in American history. Every penny was secured by one man and directed towards an insidious plot to pack our courts with right-wing extremists. A plan so methodical and calculated, that it unraveled over the course of 30 years in complete darkness.
The architect of this coup is named Leonard Leo and if you've never heard of him, that is exactly how he wants it.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001TYyZjgulf0kzL28-X9oGkGXAHP_XCxMm2zxa2wUPhuc-IkiamvSc_2tKGz0AWqpmgG3ALoI4MVF9UtDeTxo3BEJ7Xtf1vv8LgEZgYQZZn9Vdg1DMeZ68AMoyrTzgQTQPnQXarWOC4iTteUQDGjxjowdSc9BKrVsRvulxKCU7dn4H-OtskjOTRn26sOtpRR3GAfPrG3vin6zd5a_tgmxwA8uB_VZwRh0pqYEItsm9-bLVM7ypOtdvNncqbMi_rSrB&c=NjKxPCM3Ur_7cHyJKXeWPbZFuATyc3In0hTkUwjCBOPeDrglEXsmEA==&ch=rZRL669YNtD6sDOXRWNCA2bOV54hFdj1ymkBXDqvi6lHJagUaK85VQ==)
---
Who is Leonard Leo?
He has never appeared on a ballot. He does not seek the spotlight. He is the Chairman of the Federalist Society and operates in the shadows. And from those shadows he has done incomprehensible damage to American democracy.
Leonard Leo built the Supreme Court's extremist conservative majority. He placed Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, and Barrett on the court. And when Trump gets to replace two or three of the oldest justices, which he is already preparing to do, Leonard Leo will choose their replacements.
Here is what Leo's court has already delivered: Roe overturned. Trump granted criminal immunity. Citizens United enabled. The Voting Rights Act gutted. Federal regulatory power dismantled. That is not a full list. It is barely the beginning.
Leonard Leo is the reason you are angry. He's the reason for our polarized politics, the corruption with no accountability, the rights that have been stripped away, the dysfunction that feels permanent. He did not cause all of it. But he built the judicial infrastructure that made all of it possible, and that is making all of it permanent.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001TYyZjgulf0kzL28-X9oGkGXAHP_XCxMm2zxa2wUPhuc-IkiamvSc_2tKGz0AWqpmgG3ALoI4MVF9UtDeTxo3BEJ7Xtf1vv8LgEZgYQZZn9Vdg1DMeZ68AMoyrTzgQTQPnQXarWOC4iTteUQDGjxjowdSc9BKrVsRvulxKCU7dn4H-OtskjOTRn26sOtpRR3GAfPrG3vin6zd5a_tgmxwA8uB_VZwRh0pqYEItsm9-bIkBEVHBeWYfDD4oU3E9NAu&c=NjKxPCM3Ur_7cHyJKXeWPbZFuATyc3In0hTkUwjCBOPeDrglEXsmEA==&ch=rZRL669YNtD6sDOXRWNCA2bOV54hFdj1ymkBXDqvi6lHJagUaK85VQ==)
---
And then he came for the states.
Leo spent a decade doing to state Supreme Courts exactly what he did to SCOTUS, because state courts decide voting rights, reproductive freedom, and the maps that determine who controls Congress. We were watching. We beat his machine in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin. Both times he came with his network and his money. Both times we beat him.
The state court firewall is essential. But it is not enough while Leo's Supreme Court keeps changing the rules. The only permanent answer is to unpack the court he built, and the Constitution gives us that power. Congress has changed the number of justices seven times. No amendment required.
Leo has a thirty year head start, billions in dark money cash, and a Supreme Court that has already chosen his side. But we have hundreds of thousands of Democrats who have pitched in to defeat him twice. We like our odds.
But we need you with us for what comes next: the Kansas ballot initiative, November Supreme Court elections, the 2026 midterms, and the sustained campaign to reform the court that made all of this possible.
